extraction.body: International governments and agencies have urged websites to address two critical cyber-security flaws in a programming language which powers much of the internet. The vulnerabilities were found within the PHP programming language, with a fix issued on Wednesday afternoon. Multiple cyber-security agencies have urged organisations unable to apply fixes in time to consider taking their sites down, leading bodies such as the Finnish government, Edinburgh council and the BBC to take pages offline. The flaws were discovered by AI, with cyber-security firm Wiz saying they were the "most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered" by the tech, which is reshaping the cyber landscape. Finland has temporarily shut down the government's public web services, while the Netherlands' cyber-security agency said it was taking its own website offline due to the vulnerabilities. The US National Security Agency issued similar advice on X , external for organisations to take their systems offline if they were unable to update with the fix. "These vulnerabilities often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database," it wrote. The Wikimedia Foundation, which runs the online encyclopedia Wikipedia, said it was addressing the security vulnerabilities. "We have taken down a number of other systems as a precautionary measure until they can be safely patched," it said. That led some people to be unable to access parts of Wikipedia on Wednesday. They have not confirmed a link to PHP - BBC News has approached them for comment. Other websites, including the art platform DeviantArt, have said they are " temporarily down for maintenance , external " without specifying the reason. The vulnerabilities were discovered by cyber-security researchers at the firms Calif and Wiz. Through that program, they were given access to the AI company's advanced AI tools in order to find and fix flaws in web development language. OpenAI said in a blog post , external that the discovery was "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory". It added an internal researcher at the company had also discovered the issue around the same time as the other firms. The flaws had gone undetected for more than a decade. By August, after a few weeks of using advanced AI tools, they were discovered. "Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours," Wiz said in a blog post. It has estimated "roughly 70%" of the internet is affected, though the BBC is unable to verify that figure. It forced PHP Foundation to rush out its announcement of the vulnerability and its huge scale. The Netherlands' National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, an agency of the Dutch government, has taken down its website. Similarly the website of the Tweede Kamer, the lower house of the nation's parliament, has become inaccessible. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), as well as its counterparts in the EU and Australia have urged those who use PHP to apply the fixes. "Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated," the NCSC said in a note , external . Japan's national cyber-security office and EU cyber-security officials have issued a similar warning , external . "PHP is everywhere. It ​quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful ⁠lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," cyber-security company Huntress said. Cyber-security expert Don Smith, from the Sophos Counter Threat Unit, told the BBC this would "likely be a priority target" for hackers. The immediate challenge was not simply installing a patch to fix the issue, but finding and managing every instance where PHP was running, he said. "The use of PHP is pervasive, it can sit beneath public websites, content management systems, hosting platforms and third-party products, sometimes without even being obvious to the organisation using it," he said. He said it was crucial that organisations looked out for signs that an attacker "might have already have gained a foothold". The European Union Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-EU) said the risk scores given to the vulnerabilities "indicate the potential for unauthenticated remote code execution". Such a cyber-attack could potentially allow hackers to install malware and take down websites. Dane Knecht, chief technology officer at internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, said he was , external "seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up". The NCSC said once organisations have installed the update, they should "continuously monitor for security updates from third-party software vendors, including for appliances and services that may bundle PHP". It is not yet clear which versions of the programming language are affected, but CERT-EU said it could affect all versions of it dating back to PHP 5 onwards - which launched in 2004. extraction.body: WEBSITES around the world – including in Scotland – remain offline after a researcher using AI discovered a "critical security issue" in a programming language. The flaws were found within the PHP programming language , which powers much of the internet. PHP is used by almost 70% of websites, according to cybersecurity firm Cloudflare, and underpins popular platforms such as WordPress and Magento. Websites linked to the French, Danish, Finnish and Dutch governments are among those to appear to go offline on Wednesday afternoon in an attempt to protect their systems. NHS Scotland, several NHS boards and at least eight councils have also been affected. At the time of writing, the NHS Scotland website remains offline, with a message stating that the site is "undergoing scheduled maintenance". A screenshot from the NHS Scotland website (Image: NHS Scotland) Meanwhile, websites linked to the French, Danish, Finnish and Dutch governments are among those which went offline on Wednesday afternoon in an attempt to protect their systems. According to Cloudflare chief executive Matthew Prince, there was a dramatic surge in attempts to exploit the issue once it was announced. He wrote on Twitter/X: “Some stats on #php2shell. In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the @Cloudflare network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it. “That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now.” The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) said it had followed guidance to take its website offline, “in view of the critical security issues affecting PHP”. It is understood some of the UK Government ’s online services may be temporarily unavailable while steps are taken to maintain security, but any impact is expected to be minimal. Scottish Secretary Douglas Alexander has said the security of next week’s UK Government Budget has not been compromised by the critical security flaw. He was asked whether the issues identified with PHP could result in major Budget leaks because the OBR had to take down its website. Alexander told Times Radio: “No, I’ve had no indication whatsoever that there’s any problem in terms of a breach of Budget security. “Indeed John Healey, who I was with yesterday in Scotland, as I understand it initiated new security protocols reflecting his experience in the Ministry of Defence when he came to the Treasury as Chancellor in the summer.” Last year, the OBR’s Budget analysis was mistakenly published online ahead of then-chancellor’s Rachel Reeves statemen t to the Commons , allowing for early access to market sensitive information. Organisations have been urged by the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) to update to a new, fixed version of the software. If software cannot be immediately upgraded, organisations should consider taking their websites offline, the NCSC said. A UK Government spokesperson said: “Work is already under way across Government to actively identify and patch any potential exposure. “We encourage all organisations, private and public, large and small, to follow guidance issued by the NCSC to understand their exposure and take the necessary actions to safeguard their systems.” An expert has also warned that the flaw in the PHP programming language was revealed “earlier than it was supposed to have been”, which means hackers started checking websites to see if they could exploit the vulnerability. Speaking to BBC Radio 4’s Today programme, computer science professor Alan Woodward said: “The cat was let out of the bag rather earlier than it was supposed to have been. “There was an embargo on this, and there’s always a window between the flaw being publicly known about and it being patched so that the attackers can’t successfully get in. “And what happened, unfortunately, the day before the patch was out, somebody let the cat out of the bag. “There was an initial version of the patch that was released, and so it was very easy to compare the original with the patched version and see which bit of code you needed to go and exploit. “And that people like Amazon, Cloudflare, all sorts of companies that monitor what’s going on on the web, saw that this was being probed for. extraction.body: International governments and agencies have urged websites to address two critical cyber-security flaws in a programming language which powers much of the internet. The vulnerabilities were found within the PHP programming language, with a fix issued on Wednesday afternoon. Multiple cyber-security agencies have urged organisations unable to apply fixes in time to consider taking their sites down, leading bodies such as the Finnish government, Edinburgh council and the BBC to take pages offline. The flaws were discovered by AI, with cyber-security firm Wiz saying they were the "most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered" by the tech, which is reshaping the cyber landscape. Finland has temporarily shut down the government's public web services, while the Netherlands' cyber-security agency said it was taking its own website offline due to the vulnerabilities. The US National Security Agency issued similar advice on X , external for organisations to take their systems offline if they were unable to update with the fix. "These vulnerabilities often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database," it wrote. The Wikimedia Foundation, which runs the online encyclopedia Wikipedia, said it was addressing the security vulnerabilities. "We have taken down a number of other systems as a precautionary measure until they can be safely patched," it said. That led some people to be unable to access parts of Wikipedia on Wednesday. They have not confirmed a link to PHP - BBC News has approached them for comment. Other websites, including the art platform DeviantArt, have said they are " temporarily down for maintenance , external " without specifying the reason. The vulnerabilities were discovered by cyber-security researchers at the firms Calif and Wiz. Through that program, they were given access to the AI company's advanced AI tools in order to find and fix flaws in web development language. OpenAI said in a blog post , external that the discovery was "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory". It added an internal researcher at the company had also discovered the issue around the same time as the other firms. The flaws had gone undetected for more than a decade. By August, after a few weeks of using advanced AI tools, they were discovered. "Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours," Wiz said in a blog post. It has estimated "roughly 70%" of the internet is affected, though the BBC is unable to verify that figure. It forced PHP Foundation to rush out its announcement of the vulnerability and its huge scale. The Netherlands' National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, an agency of the Dutch government, has taken down its website. Similarly the website of the Tweede Kamer, the lower house of the nation's parliament, has become inaccessible. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), as well as its counterparts in the EU and Australia have urged those who use PHP to apply the fixes. "Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated," the NCSC said in a note , external . Japan's national cyber-security office and EU cyber-security officials have issued a similar warning , external . "PHP is everywhere. It ​quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful ⁠lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," cyber-security company Huntress said. Cyber-security expert Don Smith, from the Sophos Counter Threat Unit, told the BBC this would "likely be a priority target" for hackers. The immediate challenge was not simply installing a patch to fix the issue, but finding and managing every instance where PHP was running, he said. "The use of PHP is pervasive, it can sit beneath public websites, content management systems, hosting platforms and third-party products, sometimes without even being obvious to the organisation using it," he said. He said it was crucial that organisations looked out for signs that an attacker "might have already have gained a foothold". The European Union Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-EU) said the risk scores given to the vulnerabilities "indicate the potential for unauthenticated remote code execution". Such a cyber-attack could potentially allow hackers to install malware and take down websites. Dane Knecht, chief technology officer at internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, said he was , external "seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up". The NCSC said once organisations have installed the update, they should "continuously monitor for security updates from third-party software vendors, including for appliances and services that may bundle PHP". It is not yet clear which versions of the programming language are affected, but CERT-EU said it could affect all versions of it dating back to PHP 5 onwards - which launched in 2004. extraction.body: WEBSITES around the world – including in Scotland – remain offline after a researcher using AI discovered a "critical security issue" in a programming language. The flaws were found within the PHP programming language , which powers much of the internet. PHP is used by almost 70% of websites, according to cybersecurity firm Cloudflare, and underpins popular platforms such as WordPress and Magento. Websites linked to the French, Danish, Finnish and Dutch governments are among those to appear to go offline on Wednesday afternoon in an attempt to protect their systems. NHS Scotland, several NHS boards and at least eight councils have also been affected. At the time of writing, the NHS Scotland website remains offline, with a message stating that the site is "undergoing scheduled maintenance". A screenshot from the NHS Scotland website (Image: NHS Scotland) Meanwhile, websites linked to the French, Danish, Finnish and Dutch governments are among those which went offline on Wednesday afternoon in an attempt to protect their systems. According to Cloudflare chief executive Matthew Prince, there was a dramatic surge in attempts to exploit the issue once it was announced. He wrote on Twitter/X: “Some stats on #php2shell. In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the @Cloudflare network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it. “That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now.” The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) said it had followed guidance to take its website offline, “in view of the critical security issues affecting PHP”. It is understood some of the UK Government ’s online services may be temporarily unavailable while steps are taken to maintain security, but any impact is expected to be minimal. Scottish Secretary Douglas Alexander has said the security of next week’s UK Government Budget has not been compromised by the critical security flaw. He was asked whether the issues identified with PHP could result in major Budget leaks because the OBR had to take down its website. Alexander told Times Radio: “No, I’ve had no indication whatsoever that there’s any problem in terms of a breach of Budget security. “Indeed John Healey, who I was with yesterday in Scotland, as I understand it initiated new security protocols reflecting his experience in the Ministry of Defence when he came to the Treasury as Chancellor in the summer.” Last year, the OBR’s Budget analysis was mistakenly published online ahead of then-chancellor’s Rachel Reeves statemen t to the Commons , allowing for early access to market sensitive information. Organisations have been urged by the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) to update to a new, fixed version of the software. If software cannot be immediately upgraded, organisations should consider taking their websites offline, the NCSC said. A UK Government spokesperson said: “Work is already under way across Government to actively identify and patch any potential exposure. “We encourage all organisations, private and public, large and small, to follow guidance issued by the NCSC to understand their exposure and take the necessary actions to safeguard their systems.” An expert has also warned that the flaw in the PHP programming language was revealed “earlier than it was supposed to have been”, which means hackers started checking websites to see if they could exploit the vulnerability. Speaking to BBC Radio 4’s Today programme, computer science professor Alan Woodward said: “The cat was let out of the bag rather earlier than it was supposed to have been. “There was an embargo on this, and there’s always a window between the flaw being publicly known about and it being patched so that the attackers can’t successfully get in. “And what happened, unfortunately, the day before the patch was out, somebody let the cat out of the bag. “There was an initial version of the patch that was released, and so it was very easy to compare the original with the patched version and see which bit of code you needed to go and exploit. “And that people like Amazon, Cloudflare, all sorts of companies that monitor what’s going on on the web, saw that this was being probed for. sources.title: PHP2Shell: AI uncovers critical RCE vulnerabilities affecting 70% of the Internet - wiz.io
passages: With 70% of the Internet affected, the impact of PHP2Shell cannot be overstated.
The vulnerable code had been there for more than a decade – what AI changed was the ability to understand the weaknesses and turn them into a working exploit.
With frontier AI models and the right tools, a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work.
Some vulnerabilities become turning points because they challenge fundamental assumptions about security.
In 2014, Heartbleed exposed the fragility of shared infrastructure securing the internet.
In 2021, Log4Shell revealed how deeply embedded software dependencies could create widespread exposure that organizations struggled to identify.
We believe PHP2Shell could mark a similar turning point for the AI era, illustrating how AI can change the practical exploitability of longstanding vulnerabilities.
Building the exploit required chaining multiple flaws and adapting to each target’s memory layout through repeated testing and debugging.
Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours.
As the time and expertise required for this work decrease, complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier, changing how we define what is vulnerable in practice.
Wiz Research uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in core PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world.
Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them.
Sensor customers using the newest version (1.0.12768) can also enable a built-in response policy to automatically terminate processes exhibiting behaviors typical of PHP2Shell exploitation:
Notably, Gemini 4 Argon made an invaluable contribution to finding the vulnerability, exploit development, attack detection, and validation of the patch.

Wiz customers should refer to the Wiz Threat Intel Center advisory for PHP2Shell , which includes built-in coverage for agentless and runtime vulnerability detection, exploitation detection via Wiz Defend and Sensor, and automatic response policies, alongside remediation and threat hunting guidance.

These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it , putting every affected website in immediate risk.
Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4.
Below you can find a table that demonstrates what type of impact was demonstrated by each of the bugs we reported to PHP.
The applications listed below are targets we chose for the RCE demonstrations.
Demonstrations of PHP2Shell with Wordpress, Joomla, and Drupal:
For over a decade, these critical vulnerabilities remained unaddressed because vulnerability discovery and exploitation were incredibly complex.
August 24, 2026: Wiz Research reports the vulnerabilities to the PHP security team.

We combined these vulnerabilities into a single exploit script, php2shell, and demonstrated that it could execute code remotely without authentication on deployments of WordPress ( wordpress:latest ), Drupal ( drupal:latest ), and Joomla ( joomla:latest ), using their latest container images at the time of testing.
Wiz researchers will walk through what we've discovered, how we found these vulnerabilities, and what security teams need to know to assess their exposure and respond.

Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them. These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it , putting every affected website in immediate risk. Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4. Attackers can exploit them remotely, in some cases fairly easily. Immediate patching is strongly advised. On October 21, 2026, PHP released the patch fixing multiple memory-safety vulnerabilities in the core engine. These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history. The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit. In this post, we explain how frontier AI helped us find and fix vulnerabilities that had remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade. The issues described below all stem from key architecture decisions, some made over a decade ago, and were grouped under two CVEs, with severity reaching CVSS 9.2. The work grew into a cross-industry effort to protect customers, find variants, deploy detections and mitigations, and verify a patch in time for coordinated disclosure. Nearly every PHP version is affected by at least one of these issues, including releases dating back to PHP 5.4. The vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on affected servers or read sensitive process memory. Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours. As the time and expertise required for this work decrease, complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier, changing how we define what is vulnerable in practice. The WordPress, Drupal and Joomla chains are representative demonstrations. The underlying primitives exist at the PHP engine level and can affect any PHP application running on a vulnerable version.

These issues execute below the application layer, so application logs may contain little context. Until systems are patched, defenders should pay particular attention to unusual multipart requests followed by memory-limit errors or repeated HTTP 500 responses, unexpectedly large or malformed PHPSESSID response cookies, and unexplained PHP worker churn. These signals can guide an investigation. Applying the PHP security update remains the only complete remediation.

PHP parses RFC1867 multipart requests during request startup, before normal module initialization has completed. Session upload-progress handling can initialize Session state at this early stage and publish a session ID in PS(id) . An out-of-memory error can abort the request before cleanup completes. PHP then destroys the request heap and may leave PS(id) pointing to the freed allocation.

This changes the economics of both discovery and exploitation. Vulnerabilities that once seemed impractical to exploit become viable targets. These same capabilities also give defenders a chance to uncover and fix flaws that have survived years of scrutiny.

Wiz researchers will walk through what we've discovered, how we found these vulnerabilities, and what security teams need to know to assess their exposure and respond.

passages: Two critical flaws in the PHP language itself, together nicknamed PHP2Shell, now have emergency fixes.

Help Net Security reports the PHP team has released updates for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which let attackers run code on a web server without logging in, and that the fixes ship in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35.
Because PHP sits underneath WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento, AppleInsider expects a few days of patching, and with it some website outages.

Because PHP sits underneath WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento, AppleInsider expects a few days of patching, and with it some website outages. Found us on Google? Add tbreak as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Top Stories. The PHP security team rates both flaws CVSS v4.0 9.2. The bugs sit in the interpreter, not in any one app. Patchstack says that means any site on a vulnerable PHP version is exposed, whatever CMS or framework it runs. The first bug, CVE-2026-109618, comes from out-of-memory handling. If PHP runs out of memory while setting up request data, that data is left partly initialised, and request cleanup then treats it as valid, opening a path to code execution. The second, CVE-2026-109619, is a stale-state problem. Request-owned internal state can survive after its memory has been freed, so a later request handled by the same worker may use it before normal initialisation resets it. The reach is wide. Wiz Research, which reported the bugs to PHP, says every version back to 5.4 is affected by at least one of the issues. Wiz demonstrated unauthenticated code execution against the latest WordPress, Drupal and Joomla container images, and says even a “Hello World” app on a vulnerable version can be exploited. It also showed it could read PHP worker memory, which can hold passwords, tokens and API keys. Help Net Security says the affected setups include PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed, with mod_php the riskiest, and that a working exploit can trigger the attack with one unauthenticated request before any application code runs. In a write-up , Wiz researchers called the findings among the most severe ever discovered in PHP. They also said frontier AI models lowered the barrier to turning a decades-old flaw into a working exploit, a claim we haven’t independently verified. The timeline went wrong early. The CVE identifiers circulated on Hacker News and social media on 20 October, and later that day the PHP security team published an advance notice of a release set for 21 October at 14:00 UTC. According to watchTowr, the flaws were originally due to be disclosed under embargo on Thursday, 22 October. Exploitation followed the leak. Patchstack says the flaw is already being actively exploited and lists multiple confirmed incidents. WatchTowr says its honeypot network observed exploitation in the wild as of 21 October. Security researcher Kevin Beaumont, quoted by Help Net Security, said the situation will lead to “a mass of incidents”. Regulators have also stepped in. CERT-EU published an advisory naming both CVEs. AppleInsider, citing Reuters , says EU cybersecurity officials told organisations that can’t apply the fixes to be ready to take PHP sites offline temporarily. The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre is urging the same for any system that can’t be fixed right away. The cure is an upgrade. Help Net Security says Linux distributions and long-term support vendors received the patches ahead of the public release, so admins should check their vendor for updated packages. Anyone relying on the volunteer-run rpms.remirepo.net repository won’t find updates there today, and the report advises switching to distribution packages or building from source. Older branches are the awkward part. Help Net Security says PHP no longer supports 8.1 and earlier, though some distributions and LTS vendors offer backported fixes. The PHP security team also released minimal source backports for PHP 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1, aimed at people who build from source or have no LTS vendor. Tenable’s pre-release FAQ expected end-of-life branches to get no fixes, so an upgrade to a supported release is the safer route. If you can’t patch immediately, a web application firewall can buy time. Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht said in a post on X that PHP sites behind Cloudflare already have an initial set of WAF rules for the known exploit vectors, available to all customers including free plans. Patchstack is blunt that only an update is a complete fix. For everyone else, there’s little to do. AppleInsider says no patches are needed for browsers or apps, so ordinary users can only wait out any downtime and avoid entering credentials on sites that look broken or half-restored. Hal Pomeranz, a forensics expert quoted by Help Net Security, expects a long tail of forgotten, unmaintained installs that never get fixed. No. AppleInsider says browsers and apps need no patches, because the flaws are on the server side. The practical effect is that some sites may go down or behave oddly while their owners patch. Update PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, depending on your branch. On shared or managed hosting, ask your provider to confirm they’ve applied the patched packages. We recommend doing that today rather than waiting for a plugin or CMS update, since the bug is in PHP, not in WordPress itself. Contact your distribution or LTS vendor to ask whether they’ve backported the fix, or move to a supported PHP release. The PHP team has also published minimal source backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 if you build from source. If none of that is possible, CERT-EU and the NCSC both advise taking the affected system offline until it’s fixed. UAE tech, gaming and entertainment — trusted for 25 years. Older branches are the awkward part. Help Net Security says PHP no longer supports 8.1 and earlier, though some distributions and LTS vendors offer backported fixes. The PHP security team also released minimal source backports for PHP 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1, aimed at people who build from source or have no LTS vendor. Tenable’s pre-release FAQ expected end-of-life branches to get no fixes, so an upgrade to a supported release is the safer route.

Patchstack is blunt that only an update is a complete fix.

For everyone else, there’s little to do. AppleInsider says no patches are needed for browsers or apps, so ordinary users can only wait out any downtime and avoid entering credentials on sites that look broken or half-restored. Hal Pomeranz, a forensics expert quoted by Help Net Security, expects a long tail of forgotten, unmaintained installs that never get fixed.
No. AppleInsider says browsers and apps need no patches, because the flaws are on the server side. The practical effect is that some sites may go down or behave oddly while their owners patch.

Update PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, depending on your branch. On shared or managed hosting, ask your provider to confirm they’ve applied the patched packages. We recommend doing that today rather than waiting for a plugin or CMS update, since the bug is in PHP, not in WordPress itself.

Contact your distribution or LTS vendor to ask whether they’ve backported the fix, or move to a supported PHP release. The PHP team has also published minimal source backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 if you build from source. If none of that is possible, CERT-EU and the NCSC both advise taking the affected system offline until it’s fixed.

coreStoryFacts.text: The PHP development team has released emergency security updates to fix PHP2Shell, two critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) that could let attackers execute code remotely on web servers without logging in.
The fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, and the team is strongly urging all PHP users to update immediately.
According to Amazon Threat Intelligence, its MadPot honeypot network recorded a PHP2Shell exploitation attempt on Oct.
The attempt came from an IP address tied to a commercial anonymization service.

Because the vulnerabilities were still under embargo at the time, Amazon believes a threat actor was behind the activity, given that it targeted a honeypot and was routed through an anonymized address.
How the attacker obtained exploit details before disclosure is still unknown.
Palo Alto Networks confirmed that all versions of PAN-OS and Panorama are affected by PHP2Shell.
With 70% of the Internet affected, the impact of PHP2Shell cannot be overstated.
The vulnerable code had been there for more than a decade – what AI changed was the ability to understand the weaknesses and turn them into a working exploit.
With frontier AI models and the right tools, a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work.
Some vulnerabilities become turning points because they challenge fundamental assumptions about security.
In 2014, Heartbleed exposed the fragility of shared infrastructure securing the internet.
In 2021, Log4Shell revealed how deeply embedded software dependencies could create widespread exposure that organizations struggled to identify.
We believe PHP2Shell could mark a similar turning point for the AI era, illustrating how AI can change the practical exploitability of longstanding vulnerabilities.
Building the exploit required chaining multiple flaws and adapting to each target’s memory layout through repeated testing and debugging.
Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours.
As the time and expertise required for this work decrease, complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier, changing how we define what is vulnerable in practice.
Wiz Research uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in core PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world.
Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them.
Sensor customers using the newest version (1.0.12768) can also enable a built-in response policy to automatically terminate processes exhibiting behaviors typical of PHP2Shell exploitation:
Notably, Gemini 4 Argon made an invaluable contribution to finding the vulnerability, exploit development, attack detection, and validation of the patch.

Wiz customers should refer to the Wiz Threat Intel Center advisory for PHP2Shell , which includes built-in coverage for agentless and runtime vulnerability detection, exploitation detection via Wiz Defend and Sensor, and automatic response policies, alongside remediation and threat hunting guidance.

These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it , putting every affected website in immediate risk.
Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4.

sources.title: PHP2Shell: AI uncovers critical RCE vulnerabilities affecting 70% of the Internet - wiz.io
passages: With 70% of the Internet affected, the impact of PHP2Shell cannot be overstated.
The vulnerable code had been there for more than a decade – what AI changed was the ability to understand the weaknesses and turn them into a working exploit.
With frontier AI models and the right tools, a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work.
Some vulnerabilities become turning points because they challenge fundamental assumptions about security.
In 2014, Heartbleed exposed the fragility of shared infrastructure securing the internet.
In 2021, Log4Shell revealed how deeply embedded software dependencies could create widespread exposure that organizations struggled to identify.
We believe PHP2Shell could mark a similar turning point for the AI era, illustrating how AI can change the practical exploitability of longstanding vulnerabilities.
Building the exploit required chaining multiple flaws and adapting to each target’s memory layout through repeated testing and debugging.
Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours.
As the time and expertise required for this work decrease, complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier, changing how we define what is vulnerable in practice.
Wiz Research uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in core PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world.
Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them.
Sensor customers using the newest version (1.0.12768) can also enable a built-in response policy to automatically terminate processes exhibiting behaviors typical of PHP2Shell exploitation:
Notably, Gemini 4 Argon made an invaluable contribution to finding the vulnerability, exploit development, attack detection, and validation of the patch.

Wiz customers should refer to the Wiz Threat Intel Center advisory for PHP2Shell , which includes built-in coverage for agentless and runtime vulnerability detection, exploitation detection via Wiz Defend and Sensor, and automatic response policies, alongside remediation and threat hunting guidance.

These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it , putting every affected website in immediate risk.
Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4.
Below you can find a table that demonstrates what type of impact was demonstrated by each of the bugs we reported to PHP.
The applications listed below are targets we chose for the RCE demonstrations.
Demonstrations of PHP2Shell with Wordpress, Joomla, and Drupal:
For over a decade, these critical vulnerabilities remained unaddressed because vulnerability discovery and exploitation were incredibly complex.
August 24, 2026: Wiz Research reports the vulnerabilities to the PHP security team.

We combined these vulnerabilities into a single exploit script, php2shell, and demonstrated that it could execute code remotely without authentication on deployments of WordPress ( wordpress:latest ), Drupal ( drupal:latest ), and Joomla ( joomla:latest ), using their latest container images at the time of testing.
Wiz researchers will walk through what we've discovered, how we found these vulnerabilities, and what security teams need to know to assess their exposure and respond.

extraction.body: Core PHP engine flaws enable remote code execution and Heartbleed-style memory disclosure across the web. Wiz Research uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in core PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world. Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them. PHP is a backbone of the web: it’s the programming language powering WordPress, Joomla, Drupal, Wikipedia’s MediaWiki, and many others. These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it , putting every affected website in immediate risk. Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4. Attackers can exploit them remotely, in some cases fairly easily. Immediate patching is strongly advised. On October 21, 2026, PHP released the patch fixing multiple memory-safety vulnerabilities in the core engine. These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history. The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit. In this post, we explain how frontier AI helped us find and fix vulnerabilities that had remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade. The issues described below all stem from key architecture decisions, some made over a decade ago, and were grouped under two CVEs, with severity reaching CVSS 9.2. The work grew into a cross-industry effort to protect customers, find variants, deploy detections and mitigations, and verify a patch in time for coordinated disclosure. Nearly every PHP version is affected by at least one of these issues, including releases dating back to PHP 5.4. The vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on affected servers or read sensitive process memory. That memory may contain passwords, authentication tokens, API keys and certificates belonging to other requests or the server itself. PHP is the programming language behind much of the web, powering WordPress, Drupal and MediaWiki, the software that runs Wikipedia. A flaw in its core engine can affect websites across this ecosystem, even when their own application code is secure. Some vulnerabilities become turning points because they challenge fundamental assumptions about security. In 2014, Heartbleed exposed the fragility of shared infrastructure securing the internet. In 2021, Log4Shell revealed how deeply embedded software dependencies could create widespread exposure that organizations struggled to identify. We believe PHP2Shell could mark a similar turning point for the AI era, illustrating how AI can change the practical exploitability of longstanding vulnerabilities. Building the exploit required chaining multiple flaws and adapting to each target’s memory layout through repeated testing and debugging. Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours. As the time and expertise required for this work decrease, complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier, changing how we define what is vulnerable in practice. OpenAI and Calif also published blogs containing details on the vulnerability – its history, technical details, and insight into the disclosure process. PHP posted as well. We’d also like to express our sincere gratitude towards Automattic, Akamai, AWS, Cloudflare , Fastly , Google , Imperva, Microsoft, Vercel , and many others, for helping prepare guidance and out-of-the-box mitigations for customers who cannot apply the patch immediately. All of the disclosed vulnerabilities are memory-safety issues that stem from bugs in how PHP handles fatal errors while processing requests, particularly out-of-memory errors. These bugs can leave a corrupted internal PHP state behind after a request ends unexpectedly. A later request or worker can reuse that stale state, leading to memory disclosure or corruption. Below you can find a table that demonstrates what type of impact was demonstrated by each of the bugs we reported to PHP. The applications listed below are targets we chose for the RCE demonstrations. They are representative targets - exploitation does not require one of these CMSs, as the vulnerable code is in PHP itself. These variants have different requirements for exploitation and can lead to different types of impact. In any case, the patch provided by the PHP team fixes the issue at its core and eliminates all variants in the patched release. For over a decade, these critical vulnerabilities remained unaddressed because vulnerability discovery and exploitation were incredibly complex. We're pleased to see Gemini 4 Argon help defenders bridge that gap, finding vulnerabilities and helping patch them. Reducing exposure before the technical details became public required coordinated work across that entire ecosystem. The WordPress, Drupal and Joomla chains are representative demonstrations. The underlying primitives exist at the PHP engine level and can affect any PHP application running on a vulnerable version. These issues execute below the application layer, so application logs may contain little context. Until systems are patched, defenders should pay particular attention to unusual multipart requests followed by memory-limit errors or repeated HTTP 500 responses, unexpectedly large or malformed PHPSESSID response cookies, and unexplained PHP worker churn. passages: Two critical flaws in the PHP language itself, together nicknamed PHP2Shell, now have emergency fixes.

Help Net Security reports the PHP team has released updates for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which let attackers run code on a web server without logging in, and that the fixes ship in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35.
Because PHP sits underneath WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento, AppleInsider expects a few days of patching, and with it some website outages.

Because PHP sits underneath WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento, AppleInsider expects a few days of patching, and with it some website outages. Found us on Google? Add tbreak as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Top Stories. The PHP security team rates both flaws CVSS v4.0 9.2. The bugs sit in the interpreter, not in any one app. Patchstack says that means any site on a vulnerable PHP version is exposed, whatever CMS or framework it runs. The first bug, CVE-2026-109618, comes from out-of-memory handling. If PHP runs out of memory while setting up request data, that data is left partly initialised, and request cleanup then treats it as valid, opening a path to code execution. The second, CVE-2026-109619, is a stale-state problem. Request-owned internal state can survive after its memory has been freed, so a later request handled by the same worker may use it before normal initialisation resets it. The reach is wide. Wiz Research, which reported the bugs to PHP, says every version back to 5.4 is affected by at least one of the issues. Wiz demonstrated unauthenticated code execution against the latest WordPress, Drupal and Joomla container images, and says even a “Hello World” app on a vulnerable version can be exploited. It also showed it could read PHP worker memory, which can hold passwords, tokens and API keys. Help Net Security says the affected setups include PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed, with mod_php the riskiest, and that a working exploit can trigger the attack with one unauthenticated request before any application code runs. In a write-up , Wiz researchers called the findings among the most severe ever discovered in PHP. They also said frontier AI models lowered the barrier to turning a decades-old flaw into a working exploit, a claim we haven’t independently verified. The timeline went wrong early. The CVE identifiers circulated on Hacker News and social media on 20 October, and later that day the PHP security team published an advance notice of a release set for 21 October at 14:00 UTC. According to watchTowr, the flaws were originally due to be disclosed under embargo on Thursday, 22 October. Exploitation followed the leak. Patchstack says the flaw is already being actively exploited and lists multiple confirmed incidents. WatchTowr says its honeypot network observed exploitation in the wild as of 21 October. Security researcher Kevin Beaumont, quoted by Help Net Security, said the situation will lead to “a mass of incidents”. Regulators have also stepped in. CERT-EU published an advisory naming both CVEs. AppleInsider, citing Reuters , says EU cybersecurity officials told organisations that can’t apply the fixes to be ready to take PHP sites offline temporarily. The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre is urging the same for any system that can’t be fixed right away. The cure is an upgrade. Help Net Security says Linux distributions and long-term support vendors received the patches ahead of the public release, so admins should check their vendor for updated packages. Anyone relying on the volunteer-run rpms.remirepo.net repository won’t find updates there today, and the report advises switching to distribution packages or building from source. Older branches are the awkward part. Help Net Security says PHP no longer supports 8.1 and earlier, though some distributions and LTS vendors offer backported fixes. The PHP security team also released minimal source backports for PHP 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1, aimed at people who build from source or have no LTS vendor. Tenable’s pre-release FAQ expected end-of-life branches to get no fixes, so an upgrade to a supported release is the safer route. If you can’t patch immediately, a web application firewall can buy time. Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht said in a post on X that PHP sites behind Cloudflare already have an initial set of WAF rules for the known exploit vectors, available to all customers including free plans. Patchstack is blunt that only an update is a complete fix. For everyone else, there’s little to do. AppleInsider says no patches are needed for browsers or apps, so ordinary users can only wait out any downtime and avoid entering credentials on sites that look broken or half-restored. Hal Pomeranz, a forensics expert quoted by Help Net Security, expects a long tail of forgotten, unmaintained installs that never get fixed. No. AppleInsider says browsers and apps need no patches, because the flaws are on the server side. The practical effect is that some sites may go down or behave oddly while their owners patch. Update PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, depending on your branch. On shared or managed hosting, ask your provider to confirm they’ve applied the patched packages. We recommend doing that today rather than waiting for a plugin or CMS update, since the bug is in PHP, not in WordPress itself. Contact your distribution or LTS vendor to ask whether they’ve backported the fix, or move to a supported PHP release. The PHP team has also published minimal source backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 if you build from source. If none of that is possible, CERT-EU and the NCSC both advise taking the affected system offline until it’s fixed. UAE tech, gaming and entertainment — trusted for 25 years. passages: According to Tesla VP for Autonomous Driving Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla owners will be able to add their own vehicles to the company’s robotaxi fleet in the second quarter of 2027.
But even if Tesla opens up its robotaxi fleet to customer-owned vehicles, major regulatory hurdles remain.
Tesla also revealed a new Robotaxi safety website, in which the company says it has driven 3.3 million miles autonomously.
The only additional requirement is to make sure that, for example, the customer Model Y can be part of the geofences and the fleet management that Tesla has for it to be fully autonomous.
Musk also said that by 2020, a “million” Tesla robotaxis would be out on the road.
Still, Tesla’s vehicle sales were down this quarter, as revenue flatlined and profits dipped.
Tesla has a few hundred Robotaxis in Texas and Florida, some of which still have human safety monitors.
Tesla might be confident it can clear every technical and legal hurdle by Q2 2027.
It’s important to mark this deadline because it’s likely that Tesla will sail right past it.
Still, Tesla has made steady, incremental strides in the tech behind its consumer driver-assistance features.
There’s also the tension between different types of Tesla owners.
When it comes to autonomous driving and robotaxis, Musk has a pretty clear pattern: he sets bold, short-term deadlines that end up slipping by years — or never happening at all.

extraction.body: For years, Elon Musk has been making big promises to Tesla owners about unsupervised autonomous driving and the ability to add their own vehicles to the company’s robotaxi fleet. During today’s third-quarter earnings call, the company finally gave itself a deadline. According to Tesla VP for Autonomous Driving Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla owners will be able to add their own vehicles to the company’s robotaxi fleet in the second quarter of 2027. Here’s his exact quote (emphasis ours): > Like I mentioned earlier, the software for Cybercabs and Model Y is the same. And pretty soon we’ll be able to release the same software as part of the V15 release to customers. The only additional requirement is to make sure that, for example, the customer Model Y can be part of the geofences and the fleet management that Tesla has for it to be fully autonomous. We suspect somewhere around Q2 next year is when we can turn on some of the first customer vehicles to be part of the robotaxi fleet. It’s important to mark this deadline because it’s likely that Tesla will sail right past it. When it comes to autonomous driving and robotaxis, Musk has a pretty clear pattern: he sets bold, short-term deadlines that end up slipping by years — or never happening at all. Still, Tesla has made steady, incremental strides in the tech behind its consumer driver-assistance features. But the long-promised goal of “unsupervised” Full Self-Driving remains unfulfilled. In 2019, Musk stood on stage at the company’s first AI Day and vowed that customer-owned vehicles could be used as part of a “Tesla Network” of robotaxis, earning their owners passive income while driving around autonomously, looking for fares. Musk also said that by 2020, a “million” Tesla robotaxis would be out on the road. Tesla has a few hundred Robotaxis in Texas and Florida, some of which still have human safety monitors. Still, FSD growth was a bright spot in Tesla’s earnings this quarter. More people buying new Teslas in North America are choosing to add Full Self-Driving (Supervised), the company reported. Over 75 percent of new buyers picked the feature this quarter — a big jump of almost 20 percentage points compared to last quarter. Still, Tesla’s vehicle sales were down this quarter, as revenue flatlined and profits dipped. Tesla also revealed a new Robotaxi safety website, in which the company says it has driven 3.3 million miles autonomously. That’s up from 380,000 unsupervised miles driven the company reported in July. But even if Tesla opens up its robotaxi fleet to customer-owned vehicles, major regulatory hurdles remain. And in most places, it’s still illegal for individuals or outside companies to use their own self-driving cars as driverless taxis or passenger rides. There’s also the tension between different types of Tesla owners. Older Model 3 and Y vehicles without the latest full-self-driving hardware suites (or AI compute infrastructure) are constrained by hardware capability. Dedicated vehicles like the Cybercab are built specifically for driverless passenger service, whereas consumer vehicles require additional software layers to guarantee safety without human intervention. Tesla might be confident it can clear every technical and legal hurdle by Q2 2027. But history says this could easily become just another deadline that quietly slips by.

sources.title: Elon Musk says Tesla will start adding vehicles it doesn’t directly own into its robotaxi network next year - Fortune
passages: Owners of Tesla cars will be able to add their vehicles to the company’s robotaxi network sometime next year, Elon Musk said on the company’s quarterly earnings call on Wednesday, potentially allowing hundreds of thousands of customers to make money by remotely renting out their cars as self-driving cabs.

Musk noted that the Tesla team hasn’t “thought hard” about the details of adding cars that it doesn’t directly own to the robotaxi service, and was still primarily focused on safety in Austin, where it debuted operations in June with a safety driver in the passenger seat.
“We need to make sure it works when the vehicles are fully under our control,” he said.
Tesla is trying to catch up with industry leader Waymo , whose fleet of self-driving robotaxis ferry paying customers in numerous U.S. cities.
Besides the technological aspect of such a plan, it’s unclear how regulatory and liability issues might come into play.

Tesla has gradually expanded its service radius in Austin (a map shared by Tesla online last week depicts the latest robotaxi service area in a distinctly phallic shape) and Musk said the company plans to expand it further in a couple weeks time.
“I’m not sure when next year, but confidently next year.”
Jessica Mathews is a former senior writer for Fortune , where she covered transportation, defense tech, and Elon Musk’s companies.
Tesla reported that revenue in its most recent quarter fell 12% year-over-year to $22.5 billion , the EV company’s worst performance in at least a decade.

The company ascribed the decline to an ongoing slump in vehicle deliveries and falling prices (trends that were not helped by Musk’s involvement in partisan politics) as well as declining revenue from environmental credits.
Teslas have driven 7,000 autonomous miles thus far since June, he said.

extraction.body: Owners of Tesla cars will be able to add their vehicles to the company’s robotaxi network sometime next year, Elon Musk said on the company’s quarterly earnings call on Wednesday, potentially allowing hundreds of thousands of customers to make money by remotely renting out their cars as self-driving cabs. “I’d say confidently next year,” Musk, the CEO of Tesla, said on the call. “I’m not sure when next year, but confidently next year.” The move would mark a major expansion of the company’s robotaxi network, which officially launched last month in Austin with just a handful of self-driving vehicles that Tesla directly owns and operates. Tesla is trying to catch up with industry leader Waymo , whose fleet of self-driving robotaxis ferry paying customers in numerous U.S. cities. Musk noted that the Tesla team hasn’t “thought hard” about the details of adding cars that it doesn’t directly own to the robotaxi service, and was still primarily focused on safety in Austin, where it debuted operations in June with a safety driver in the passenger seat. “We need to make sure it works when the vehicles are fully under our control,” he said. Tesla reported that revenue in its most recent quarter fell 12% year-over-year to $22.5 billion , the EV company’s worst performance in at least a decade. The company ascribed the decline to an ongoing slump in vehicle deliveries and falling prices (trends that were not helped by Musk’s involvement in partisan politics) as well as declining revenue from environmental credits. Musk has suggested that Tesla would eventually incorporate Tesla EVs owned by its customers into the broader robotaxi network for several months now, raising the idea that individuals would be able to rent out their own cars and eventually even manage their own fleets. Besides the technological aspect of such a plan, it’s unclear how regulatory and liability issues might come into play. And, as of now, Tesla still has yet to fully remove safety drivers from the vehicles that it owns and operates on its fledgling robotaxi service. For its initial Austin rollout , Tesla has had someone sitting in the passenger seat at all times. Tesla has gradually expanded its service radius in Austin (a map shared by Tesla online last week depicts the latest robotaxi service area in a distinctly phallic shape) and Musk said the company plans to expand it further in a couple weeks time. While Tesla’s robotaxi service is currently only available to invitees including social media influencers who regularly post about the company, and not the general public, Musk laid out lofty expansion plans for the robotaxi service on Wednesday’s earnings call, saying that Tesla was seeking regulatory permission to launch in the Bay Area, Nevada, Arizona, and Florida. “As soon as we get the approvals and we prove our safety, then we’ll be launching autonomous ride hailing in most of the country, and I think we’ll probably have autonomous ride hailing in probably half the population of the U.S. by the end of the year,” he said. So far, there have been no major safety episodes in Austin since the launch of the robotaxi service, Tesla’s CFO said on the call. Teslas have driven 7,000 autonomous miles thus far since June, he said. Jessica Mathews is a former senior writer for Fortune , where she covered transportation, defense tech, and Elon Musk’s companies.

sources.title: Musk says Tesla Semi self-driving is a year away, so truckers are safe - Electrek
passages: Elon Musk says Tesla expects to have self-driving working on the Tesla Semi “probably around the end of this year or early next year.”
If a year of Musk time on self-driving has historically meant closer to a decade, truck drivers are covered into the 2030s.

In the same answer, he said Tesla is focusing its self-driving work on its high-volume vehicles — Model 3, Model Y, and Cybercab — and that Semi autonomy is “taking a bit of a backseat for the next six months or so.”
These two statements sort of clash together because FSD won’t help with the shortage of truckers if you still need them inside the truck, just like FSD in consumer vehicles.
Ultimately, Musk is talking about full autonomy inside Tesla’s semi trucks.
The first Semi built on Tesla’s high-volume line at Giga Nevada rolled out in April .
We count roughly 10 self-driving and robotaxi deadlines since 2013, and every single one that has come due has been missed.
We charted his prediction record earlier this year using data from MuskOmeter, which tracks 94 public Musk predictions.
In July 2020, he was “100% confident” Tesla would solve Level 5 autonomy the next year.
“There just aren’t enough people around who want to drive trucks, which are crucial for transport throughout America,” he said.
Here’s the problem with a one-year Musk timeline on autonomy.
In 2022, Tesla scrubbed every mention of autonomy from its Semi marketing, and the read at the time was that Tesla needed drivers and fleet managers to want this truck.
The live promise right now is unsupervised FSD on customer cars in Q4 2026, which Musk repeated again in May and which we’ve gone through in detail .
Fred is the Editor in Chief and Main Writer at Electrek.
Last year it was robotaxi service for half the US population by December.

extraction.body: Elon Musk says Tesla expects to have self-driving working on the Tesla Semi “probably around the end of this year or early next year.” Going by Tesla’s record on self-driving deadlines, it is: their jobs are safe for a long time. The comment came on Tesla’s Q2 2026 earnings call on July 22, after LightShed analyst Walter Piecyk asked when Tesla would get around to autonomy for the Semi. Musk opened with the labor shortage. “There just aren’t enough people around who want to drive trucks, which are crucial for transport throughout America,” he said. Then he framed driverless trucks as a gift to the people who drive them: “making it easier on truck drivers to have a self-driving Semi is going to dramatically improve safety and comfort for truck drivers that use the Tesla Semi.” These two statements sort of clash together because FSD won’t help with the shortage of truckers if you still need them inside the truck, just like FSD in consumer vehicles. Ultimately, Musk is talking about full autonomy inside Tesla’s semi trucks. And the timeline: “We expect to get self-driving working on the Tesla Semi probably around the end of this year or early next year.” In the same answer, he said Tesla is focusing its self-driving work on its high-volume vehicles — Model 3, Model Y, and Cybercab — and that Semi autonomy is “taking a bit of a backseat for the next six months or so.” So it’s a year out, and nobody is really working on it for the next six months. Sure. Here’s the problem with a one-year Musk timeline on autonomy. We charted his prediction record earlier this year using data from MuskOmeter, which tracks 94 public Musk predictions. Eight of them were delivered on time. That’s 9%. Another 46 failed outright. Self-driving is his worst category. We count roughly 10 self-driving and robotaxi deadlines since 2013, and every single one that has come due has been missed. In October 2016, he said a Tesla would drive itself from Los Angeles to New York by the end of the following year. That was nine years ago and it still hasn’t happened. He said FSD would be “feature complete” by the end of 2019. He promised 1 million robotaxis on the road by 2020. In July 2020, he was “100% confident” Tesla would solve Level 5 autonomy the next year. Last year it was robotaxi service for half the US population by December. This January it was Europe and China approving FSD “next month.” The live promise right now is unsupervised FSD on customer cars in Q4 2026, which Musk repeated again in May and which we’ve gone through in detail . If a year of Musk time on self-driving has historically meant closer to a decade, truck drivers are covered into the 2030s. Tesla unveiled it in November 2017 with “Enhanced Autopilot” and a demo of convoy mode, where trucks follow each other autonomously down the highway. Production was promised for 2019. It slipped to 2020, then 2021, then 2022. A handful of trucks went to PepsiCo at the end of that year, and at the delivery event, Tesla didn’t mention Autopilot or self-driving once . Convoy mode quietly came off the website. The first Semi built on Tesla’s high-volume line at Giga Nevada rolled out in April . That factory is designed for 50,000 trucks a year. Tesla told investors this week that the Semi will still be “a very small percentage” of its total vehicle fleet by the end of 2026. The trucker-shortage framing is the part worth sitting with. In 2022, Tesla scrubbed every mention of autonomy from its Semi marketing, and the read at the time was that Tesla needed drivers and fleet managers to want this truck. Now the driverless version is back as a feature, and it’s being sold as safety and comfort for the driver whose seat it eliminates. The companies actually running driverless trucks don’t bother with that pitch. Aurora has been hauling freight on Texas highways with nobody in the cab, crossing 250,000 driverless miles in March and targeting more than 200 trucks this year. Speaking of ground-breaking tech: 2027 is the 10th anniversary of the Roadster II! Fingers crossed for an Anniversary Edition. Maybe it'll come with upgraded hover capabilities, a built-in time machine, and a delivery date set for 2045. As for Tesla, the company has racked up only 380,000 unsupervised miles in a year of testing unsupervised self-driving in its robotaxi service in Texas. And to limit the damage, the company has focused on a lower-speed, geo-fenced area. I think it will be a while before it feels confident enough to increase the speed and the geo-fenced area to a degree that it makes sense for the Tesla Semi. The honest read is that Semi autonomy is a line item Musk added because an analyst asked, then deprioritized in the same breath. It’s not a product timeline. It’s a mood. In 2022, Tesla scrubbed every mention of autonomy from its Semi marketing, and the read at the time was that Tesla needed drivers and fleet managers to want this truck. Now the driverless version is back as a feature, and it’s being sold as safety and comfort for the driver whose seat it eliminates.

The companies actually running driverless trucks don’t bother with that pitch. Aurora has been hauling freight on Texas highways with nobody in the cab, crossing 250,000 driverless miles in March and targeting more than 200 trucks this year.

Speaking of ground-breaking tech: 2027 is the 10th anniversary of the Roadster II! Fingers crossed for an Anniversary Edition. Maybe it'll come with upgraded hover capabilities, a built-in time machine, and a delivery date set for 2045.

As for Tesla, the company has racked up only 380,000 unsupervised miles in a year of testing unsupervised self-driving in its robotaxi service in Texas. And to limit the damage, the company has focused on a lower-speed, geo-fenced area.
I think it will be a while before it feels confident enough to increase the speed and the geo-fenced area to a degree that it makes sense for the Tesla Semi.
The honest read is that Semi autonomy is a line item Musk added because an analyst asked, then deprioritized in the same breath. It’s not a product timeline. It’s a mood.

coreStoryFacts.text: According to Tesla VP for Autonomous Driving Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla owners will be able to add their own vehicles to the company’s robotaxi fleet in the second quarter of 2027.
But even if Tesla opens up its robotaxi fleet to customer-owned vehicles, major regulatory hurdles remain.
Tesla also revealed a new Robotaxi safety website, in which the company says it has driven 3.3 million miles autonomously.
The only additional requirement is to make sure that, for example, the customer Model Y can be part of the geofences and the fleet management that Tesla has for it to be fully autonomous.
Musk also said that by 2020, a “million” Tesla robotaxis would be out on the road.
Still, Tesla’s vehicle sales were down this quarter, as revenue flatlined and profits dipped.
Tesla has a few hundred Robotaxis in Texas and Florida, some of which still have human safety monitors.
Tesla might be confident it can clear every technical and legal hurdle by Q2 2027.
It’s important to mark this deadline because it’s likely that Tesla will sail right past it.
Still, Tesla has made steady, incremental strides in the tech behind its consumer driver-assistance features.
There’s also the tension between different types of Tesla owners.
When it comes to autonomous driving and robotaxis, Musk has a pretty clear pattern: he sets bold, short-term deadlines that end up slipping by years — or never happening at all.

Owners of Tesla cars will be able to add their vehicles to the company’s robotaxi network sometime next year, Elon Musk said on the company’s quarterly earnings call on Wednesday, potentially allowing hundreds of thousands of customers to make money by remotely renting out their cars as self-driving cabs.

Musk noted that the Tesla team hasn’t “thought hard” about the details of adding cars that it doesn’t directly own to the robotaxi service, and was still primarily focused on safety in Austin, where it debuted operations in June with a safety driver in the passenger seat.
“We need to make sure it works when the vehicles are fully under our control,” he said.
Tesla is trying to catch up with industry leader Waymo , whose fleet of self-driving robotaxis ferry paying customers in numerous U.S. cities.
Besides the technological aspect of such a plan, it’s unclear how regulatory and liability issues might come into play.

Tesla has gradually expanded its service radius in Austin (a map shared by Tesla online last week depicts the latest robotaxi service area in a distinctly phallic shape) and Musk said the company plans to expand it further in a couple weeks time.
“I’m not sure when next year, but confidently next year.”
Jessica Mathews is a former senior writer for Fortune , where she covered transportation, defense tech, and Elon Musk’s companies.
Tesla reported that revenue in its most recent quarter fell 12% year-over-year to $22.5 billion , the EV company’s worst performance in at least a decade.

The company ascribed the decline to an ongoing slump in vehicle deliveries and falling prices (trends that were not helped by Musk’s involvement in partisan politics) as well as declining revenue from environmental credits.
Teslas have driven 7,000 autonomous miles thus far since June, he said.
Elon Musk says Tesla expects to have self-driving working on the Tesla Semi “probably around the end of this year or early next year.”

Musk noted that the Tesla team hasn’t “thought hard” about the details of adding cars that it doesn’t directly own to the robotaxi service, and was still primarily focused on safety in Austin, where it debuted operations in June with a safety driver in the passenger seat.

When it comes to autonomous driving and robotaxis, Musk has a pretty clear pattern: he sets bold, short-term deadlines that end up slipping by years — or never happening at all. Still, Tesla has made steady, incremental strides in the tech behind its consumer driver-assistance features. But the long-promised goal of “unsupervised” Full Self-Driving remains unfulfilled. In 2019, Musk stood on stage at the company’s first AI Day and vowed that customer-owned vehicles could be used as part of a “Tesla Network” of robotaxis, earning their owners passive income while driving around autonomously, looking for fares. Tesla might be confident it can clear every technical and legal hurdle by Q2 2027. But history says this could easily become just another deadline that quietly slips by.

sources.title: Elon Musk says Tesla will start adding vehicles it doesn’t directly own into its robotaxi network next year - Fortune
passages: Owners of Tesla cars will be able to add their vehicles to the company’s robotaxi network sometime next year, Elon Musk said on the company’s quarterly earnings call on Wednesday, potentially allowing hundreds of thousands of customers to make money by remotely renting out their cars as self-driving cabs.

Musk noted that the Tesla team hasn’t “thought hard” about the details of adding cars that it doesn’t directly own to the robotaxi service, and was still primarily focused on safety in Austin, where it debuted operations in June with a safety driver in the passenger seat.
“We need to make sure it works when the vehicles are fully under our control,” he said.
Tesla is trying to catch up with industry leader Waymo , whose fleet of self-driving robotaxis ferry paying customers in numerous U.S. cities.
Besides the technological aspect of such a plan, it’s unclear how regulatory and liability issues might come into play.

Tesla has gradually expanded its service radius in Austin (a map shared by Tesla online last week depicts the latest robotaxi service area in a distinctly phallic shape) and Musk said the company plans to expand it further in a couple weeks time.
“I’m not sure when next year, but confidently next year.”
Jessica Mathews is a former senior writer for Fortune , where she covered transportation, defense tech, and Elon Musk’s companies.
Tesla reported that revenue in its most recent quarter fell 12% year-over-year to $22.5 billion , the EV company’s worst performance in at least a decade.

The company ascribed the decline to an ongoing slump in vehicle deliveries and falling prices (trends that were not helped by Musk’s involvement in partisan politics) as well as declining revenue from environmental credits.
Teslas have driven 7,000 autonomous miles thus far since June, he said.
