Tesla is trying to catch up with industry leader Waymo , whose fleet of self-driving robotaxis ferry paying customers in numerous U.S. cities. Musk noted that the Tesla team hasn’t “thought hard” about the details of adding cars that it doesn’t directly own to the robotaxi service, and was still primarily focused on safety in Austin, where it debuted operations in June with a safety driver in the passenger seat. “We need to make sure it works when the vehicles are fully under our control,” he said. Tesla reported that revenue in its most recent quarter fell 12% year-over-year to $22.5 billion , the EV company’s worst performance in at least a decade. The company ascribed the decline to an ongoing slump in vehicle deliveries and falling prices (trends that were not helped by Musk’s involvement in partisan politics) as well as declining revenue from environmental credits. Musk has suggested that Tesla would eventually incorporate Tesla EVs owned by its customers into the broader robotaxi network for several months now, raising the idea that individuals would be able to rent out their own cars and eventually even manage their own fleets. Besides the technological aspect of such a plan, it’s unclear how regulatory and liability issues might come into play. And, as of now, Tesla still has yet to fully remove safety drivers from the vehicles that it owns and operates on its fledgling robotaxi service. For its initial Austin rollout , Tesla has had someone sitting in the passenger seat at all times. Tesla has gradually expanded its service radius in Austin (a map shared by Tesla online last week depicts the latest robotaxi service area in a distinctly phallic shape) and Musk said the company plans to expand it further in a couple weeks time. While Tesla’s robotaxi service is currently only available to invitees including social media influencers who regularly post about the company, and not the general public, Musk laid out lofty expansion plans for the robotaxi service on Wednesday’s earnings call, saying that Tesla was seeking regulatory permission to launch in the Bay Area, Nevada, Arizona, and Florida. “As soon as we get the approvals and we prove our safety, then we’ll be launching autonomous ride hailing in most of the country, and I think we’ll probably have autonomous ride hailing in probably half the population of the U.S. by the end of the year,” he said. So far, there have been no major safety episodes in Austin since the launch of the robotaxi service, Tesla’s CFO said on the call. Teslas have driven 7,000 autonomous miles thus far since June, he said. Jessica Mathews is a former senior writer for Fortune , where she covered transportation, defense tech, and Elon Musk’s companies.

sources.title: Musk says Tesla Semi self-driving is a year away, so truckers are safe - Electrek
passages: Elon Musk says Tesla expects to have self-driving working on the Tesla Semi “probably around the end of this year or early next year.”
If a year of Musk time on self-driving has historically meant closer to a decade, truck drivers are covered into the 2030s.

In the same answer, he said Tesla is focusing its self-driving work on its high-volume vehicles — Model 3, Model Y, and Cybercab — and that Semi autonomy is “taking a bit of a backseat for the next six months or so.”
These two statements sort of clash together because FSD won’t help with the shortage of truckers if you still need them inside the truck, just like FSD in consumer vehicles.
Ultimately, Musk is talking about full autonomy inside Tesla’s semi trucks.
The first Semi built on Tesla’s high-volume line at Giga Nevada rolled out in April .
We count roughly 10 self-driving and robotaxi deadlines since 2013, and every single one that has come due has been missed.
We charted his prediction record earlier this year using data from MuskOmeter, which tracks 94 public Musk predictions.
In July 2020, he was “100% confident” Tesla would solve Level 5 autonomy the next year.
“There just aren’t enough people around who want to drive trucks, which are crucial for transport throughout America,” he said.
Here’s the problem with a one-year Musk timeline on autonomy.
In 2022, Tesla scrubbed every mention of autonomy from its Semi marketing, and the read at the time was that Tesla needed drivers and fleet managers to want this truck.
The live promise right now is unsupervised FSD on customer cars in Q4 2026, which Musk repeated again in May and which we’ve gone through in detail .
Fred is the Editor in Chief and Main Writer at Electrek.
Last year it was robotaxi service for half the US population by December.

extraction.body: Elon Musk says Tesla expects to have self-driving working on the Tesla Semi “probably around the end of this year or early next year.” Going by Tesla’s record on self-driving deadlines, it is: their jobs are safe for a long time. The comment came on Tesla’s Q2 2026 earnings call on July 22, after LightShed analyst Walter Piecyk asked when Tesla would get around to autonomy for the Semi. Musk opened with the labor shortage. “There just aren’t enough people around who want to drive trucks, which are crucial for transport throughout America,” he said. Then he framed driverless trucks as a gift to the people who drive them: “making it easier on truck drivers to have a self-driving Semi is going to dramatically improve safety and comfort for truck drivers that use the Tesla Semi.” These two statements sort of clash together because FSD won’t help with the shortage of truckers if you still need them inside the truck, just like FSD in consumer vehicles. Ultimately, Musk is talking about full autonomy inside Tesla’s semi trucks. And the timeline: “We expect to get self-driving working on the Tesla Semi probably around the end of this year or early next year.” In the same answer, he said Tesla is focusing its self-driving work on its high-volume vehicles — Model 3, Model Y, and Cybercab — and that Semi autonomy is “taking a bit of a backseat for the next six months or so.” So it’s a year out, and nobody is really working on it for the next six months. Sure. Here’s the problem with a one-year Musk timeline on autonomy. We charted his prediction record earlier this year using data from MuskOmeter, which tracks 94 public Musk predictions. Eight of them were delivered on time. That’s 9%. Another 46 failed outright. Self-driving is his worst category. We count roughly 10 self-driving and robotaxi deadlines since 2013, and every single one that has come due has been missed. In October 2016, he said a Tesla would drive itself from Los Angeles to New York by the end of the following year. That was nine years ago and it still hasn’t happened. He said FSD would be “feature complete” by the end of 2019. He promised 1 million robotaxis on the road by 2020. In July 2020, he was “100% confident” Tesla would solve Level 5 autonomy the next year. Last year it was robotaxi service for half the US population by December. This January it was Europe and China approving FSD “next month.” The live promise right now is unsupervised FSD on customer cars in Q4 2026, which Musk repeated again in May and which we’ve gone through in detail . If a year of Musk time on self-driving has historically meant closer to a decade, truck drivers are covered into the 2030s. Tesla unveiled it in November 2017 with “Enhanced Autopilot” and a demo of convoy mode, where trucks follow each other autonomously down the highway. Production was promised for 2019. It slipped to 2020, then 2021, then 2022. A handful of trucks went to PepsiCo at the end of that year, and at the delivery event, Tesla didn’t mention Autopilot or self-driving once . Convoy mode quietly came off the website. The first Semi built on Tesla’s high-volume line at Giga Nevada rolled out in April . That factory is designed for 50,000 trucks a year. Tesla told investors this week that the Semi will still be “a very small percentage” of its total vehicle fleet by the end of 2026. The trucker-shortage framing is the part worth sitting with. In 2022, Tesla scrubbed every mention of autonomy from its Semi marketing, and the read at the time was that Tesla needed drivers and fleet managers to want this truck. Now the driverless version is back as a feature, and it’s being sold as safety and comfort for the driver whose seat it eliminates. The companies actually running driverless trucks don’t bother with that pitch. Aurora has been hauling freight on Texas highways with nobody in the cab, crossing 250,000 driverless miles in March and targeting more than 200 trucks this year. Speaking of ground-breaking tech: 2027 is the 10th anniversary of the Roadster II! Fingers crossed for an Anniversary Edition. Maybe it'll come with upgraded hover capabilities, a built-in time machine, and a delivery date set for 2045. As for Tesla, the company has racked up only 380,000 unsupervised miles in a year of testing unsupervised self-driving in its robotaxi service in Texas. And to limit the damage, the company has focused on a lower-speed, geo-fenced area. I think it will be a while before it feels confident enough to increase the speed and the geo-fenced area to a degree that it makes sense for the Tesla Semi. The honest read is that Semi autonomy is a line item Musk added because an analyst asked, then deprioritized in the same breath. It’s not a product timeline. It’s a mood. relevantPassages.text: Elon Musk says Tesla expects to have self-driving working on the Tesla Semi “probably around the end of this year or early next year.”
If a year of Musk time on self-driving has historically meant closer to a decade, truck drivers are covered into the 2030s.

In the same answer, he said Tesla is focusing its self-driving work on its high-volume vehicles — Model 3, Model Y, and Cybercab — and that Semi autonomy is “taking a bit of a backseat for the next six months or so.”
These two statements sort of clash together because FSD won’t help with the shortage of truckers if you still need them inside the truck, just like FSD in consumer vehicles.
Ultimately, Musk is talking about full autonomy inside Tesla’s semi trucks.
The first Semi built on Tesla’s high-volume line at Giga Nevada rolled out in April .
We count roughly 10 self-driving and robotaxi deadlines since 2013, and every single one that has come due has been missed.
We charted his prediction record earlier this year using data from MuskOmeter, which tracks 94 public Musk predictions.
In July 2020, he was “100% confident” Tesla would solve Level 5 autonomy the next year.
“There just aren’t enough people around who want to drive trucks, which are crucial for transport throughout America,” he said.
Here’s the problem with a one-year Musk timeline on autonomy.
In 2022, Tesla scrubbed every mention of autonomy from its Semi marketing, and the read at the time was that Tesla needed drivers and fleet managers to want this truck.
The live promise right now is unsupervised FSD on customer cars in Q4 2026, which Musk repeated again in May and which we’ve gone through in detail .
Fred is the Editor in Chief and Main Writer at Electrek.
Last year it was robotaxi service for half the US population by December.

extraction.body: Tomorrow, First. News and intelligence for the agentic economy Two critical remote code execution flaws in the PHP language runtime, found by frontier AI models after a decade of manual audits failed to catch them, put 70% of the web on notice. Frontier AI models have identified two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities in the PHP language runtime that remained undetected through a decade of manual security audits. The vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on servers running affected versions of PHP. AI-assisted analysis identified these memory-corruption flaws, which had remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade. Wiz Research , which combined these vulnerabilities into an exploit script dubbed “php2shell,” identified the flaws as memory-safety issues stemming from how PHP handles fatal errors during request processing. CVE-2026-109618 involves out-of-memory (OOM) corruption, where PHP interrupts a request while internal data is only partially initialized. During the subsequent cleanup process, the runtime incorrectly treats this invalid data as valid. CVE-2026-109619 involves stale global state, where request-owned internal state persists after its backing memory has been freed, allowing a subsequent request handled by the same worker to utilize the stale data before it is reset. Both vulnerabilities carry a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2, marking them as critical. The flaws exploit the runtime’s trust-through-defaults pattern: the engine assumes its internal state is consistent even after an interrupted request. This pattern of implicit trust in memory management is a recurring theme in recent infrastructure vulnerabilities, similar to issues previously tracked in BeyondTrust , nine-layer , and ConnectWise . Unlike the identity-layer and supply-chain trust gaps analyzed in our prior coverage, including the synthesis in the nine-layer report, PHP2Shell represents a distinct class of failure: it sits below the application layer entirely, where the language runtime blindly trusts its own internal memory state. One brief each morning, reported by the same minds who write Forkast. Wiz Research identified these vulnerabilities using Wiz Atlas, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol. According to the firm, a single researcher completed in a week what would previously have taken a world-class team months of work. Writing in the Google Cloud post she co-authored with CISO Chris Betz, Raluca Ada Popa, Head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said Gemini 4 Argon made “an invaluable contribution to finding the vulnerability, exploit development, attack detection, and validation of the patch.” Independently, researcher Ryan Austin of Calif surfaced the same bug class while auditing PHP under OpenAI’s “Patch the Planet” initiative. Calif’s write-up of the disclosure dates the first confirmed out-of-memory fatal to August 1, days into the audit, with the first bug reported to PHP on August 11 and a working exploit confirmed by the project on August 15. Wiz Research writes that the findings “rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history,” and that demonstrating exploitability required “an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve” before frontier AI models lowered that barrier. According to Wiz Research, PHP powers 70% of all websites globally, meaning the vulnerabilities affect a significant portion of the internet. The flaws impact all currently supported PHP branches, including versions 5.4 through 8.5.11, as well as older end-of-life branches. Apache mod_php represents the highest risk surface, as the exploit can succeed before any application code executes. Other environments, including PHP-FPM, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed, are also at risk. Wiz demonstrated unauthenticated RCE against the latest container images for WordPress, Drupal, and Joomla. While Google Cloud is not itself vulnerable, the company confirmed that users running PHP on its infrastructure may be exposed. The PHP security team released patches on October 21, 2026, in versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. Because PHP 8.1 and older versions are end-of-life, the project provided only minimal source-backports for versions 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1. Administrators are advised to update immediately. For systems where immediate patching is not possible, the PHP project recommends specific mitigations: setting memory_limit to -1 to address CVE-2026-109618, and setting session.upload_progress.enabled to 0 and fatal_error_backtraces to 0 to mitigate CVE-2026-109619. While eSentire’s advisory reports unverified claims of exploit code circulating in the wild, those reports remain unconfirmed. Rapid7’s emergency threat response covers the same pair; that page returned a 403 bot wall at fetch, so it is named here rather than quoted. Wiz Research , which combined these vulnerabilities into an exploit script dubbed “php2shell,” identified the flaws as memory-safety issues stemming from how PHP handles fatal errors during request processing. CVE-2026-109618 involves out-of-memory (OOM) corruption, where PHP interrupts a request while internal data is only partially initialized. During the subsequent cleanup process, the runtime incorrectly treats this invalid data as valid. CVE-2026-109619 involves stale global state, where request-owned internal state persists after its backing memory has been freed, allowing a subsequent request handled by the same worker to utilize the stale data before it is reset.

Both vulnerabilities carry a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2, marking them as critical. The flaws exploit the runtime’s trust-through-defaults pattern: the engine assumes its internal state is consistent even after an interrupted request. This pattern of implicit trust in memory management is a recurring theme in recent infrastructure vulnerabilities, similar to issues previously tracked in BeyondTrust , nine-layer , and ConnectWise . Unlike the identity-layer and supply-chain trust gaps analyzed in our prior coverage, including the synthesis in the nine-layer report, PHP2Shell represents a distinct class of failure: it sits below the application layer entirely, where the language runtime blindly trusts its own internal memory state.
One brief each morning, reported by the same minds who write Forkast.

Wiz Research identified these vulnerabilities using Wiz Atlas, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol. According to the firm, a single researcher completed in a week what would previously have taken a world-class team months of work. Writing in the Google Cloud post she co-authored with CISO Chris Betz, Raluca Ada Popa, Head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said Gemini 4 Argon made “an invaluable contribution to finding the vulnerability, exploit development, attack detection, and validation of the patch.”

Independently, researcher Ryan Austin of Calif surfaced the same bug class while auditing PHP under OpenAI’s “Patch the Planet” initiative. Calif’s write-up of the disclosure dates the first confirmed out-of-memory fatal to August 1, days into the audit, with the first bug reported to PHP on August 11 and a working exploit confirmed by the project on August 15.

Wiz Research writes that the findings “rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history,” and that demonstrating exploitability required “an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve” before frontier AI models lowered that barrier.

According to Wiz Research, PHP powers 70% of all websites globally, meaning the vulnerabilities affect a significant portion of the internet. The flaws impact all currently supported PHP branches, including versions 5.4 through 8.5.11, as well as older end-of-life branches. Apache mod_php represents the highest risk surface, as the exploit can succeed before any application code executes. Other environments, including PHP-FPM, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed, are also at risk.

Wiz demonstrated unauthenticated RCE against the latest container images for WordPress, Drupal, and Joomla. While Google Cloud is not itself vulnerable, the company confirmed that users running PHP on its infrastructure may be exposed.

The PHP security team released patches on October 21, 2026, in versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. Because PHP 8.1 and older versions are end-of-life, the project provided only minimal source-backports for versions 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1. Administrators are advised to update immediately.

For systems where immediate patching is not possible, the PHP project recommends specific mitigations: setting memory_limit to -1 to address CVE-2026-109618, and setting session.upload_progress.enabled to 0 and fatal_error_backtraces to 0 to mitigate CVE-2026-109619. While eSentire’s advisory reports unverified claims of exploit code circulating in the wild, those reports remain unconfirmed. Rapid7’s emergency threat response covers the same pair; that page returned a 403 bot wall at fetch, so it is named here rather than quoted.

extraction.body: Government and company websites around the world briefly went dark and suspended some services, as operators scrambled to patch their systems after artificial intelligence helped find critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language. The US National Security Agency and Europe’s cybersecurity agency on Wednesday advised companies to take immediate action to address two critical flaws in PHP, a programming language that powers 70% of all websites in the world, including WordPress and Drupal, an open-source content management system. The PHP Foundation, the organization behind the coding language, has released a patch for the bugs, which have been hidden in their software for years, and is urging website operators to update their systems immediately. Popular Irish news website The Journal was temporarily offline Thursday morning while it bolstered its “defences,” it said in a notice. The Journal is Ireland’s second most-used online news source, behind only RTÉ, the national broadcaster, according to the Reuters Institute. The flaws in PHP – which originally stood for Personal Home Page – were uncovered by teams at OpenAI, Google-owned cybersecurity company Wiz, and another cybersecurity company, Calif. The bugs, collectively called PHP2Shell, could allow attackers to hack into websites and read memory that could contain sensitive information, like passwords. World leaders weigh in Even world leaders urged organizations to take action. Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten said that his cabinet was “closely monitoring the situation surrounding the vulnerabilities in PHP.” Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said companies should consider suspending services if necessary in order to reduce their exposure. “Please check if your publicly available websites use PHP, and prepare to apply the fix patch that will be released tonight… as soon as possible,” she posted on X Wednesday. Japanese airline ANA, railway operator JR West and the country’s largest bank, MUFG, were among companies that reported some webpages and services temporarily suspended. In Europe, government websites in France, Denmark, Finland and the Netherlands, including the Dutch cyber security agency, were temporarily taken offline while security fixes were implemented. The Wikimedia Foundation, the non-profit that operates Wikipedia, told CNN Thursday that it was “in the process of addressing security vulnerabilities in PHP,” and that a number of its systems had been taken down as a “precautionary measure.” ‘AI inflection point’ AI played a crucial role in finding and fixing vulnerabilities “that had remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade,” according to Wiz, which said the episode marks an “AI inflection point.” “What AI changed was the ability to understand the weaknesses and turn them into a working exploit,” Wiz researchers wrote in a blog post Wednesday. “With frontier AI models and the right tools, a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work,” they added. The bugs were discovered in late August but were disclosed to the public only on Wednesday, after PHP had come up with a fix. The flaws could allow attackers to remotely execute code, disrupt services and expose customer data, according to web infrastructure provider Cloudflare, which has been working with the PHP Foundation, Calif, OpenAI and Wiz to address the issue. Researchers at Wiz used Google’s Gemini 4 Argon, Wiz Atlas and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol during the research process. Heartbleed similarities Wiz researchers say the issue is on par with the Heartbleed bug from 2014, which impacted an encryption technology estimated to be used by two-thirds of the Web. Like Heartbleed, the researchers at Wiz say PHP2Shell could similarly serve as a turning point in cybersecurity. While the vulnerabilities existed for years, AI made it practical to deploy them. “The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve,” the researchers said. “Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit.” – John Liu, Anna Cooban and Amy Croffey contributed reporting.

sources.title: PHP2Shell: AI uncovers critical RCE vulnerabilities affecting 70% of the Internet - wiz.io
passages: With 70% of the Internet affected, the impact of PHP2Shell cannot be overstated.
The vulnerable code had been there for more than a decade – what AI changed was the ability to understand the weaknesses and turn them into a working exploit.
With frontier AI models and the right tools, a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work.
Some vulnerabilities become turning points because they challenge fundamental assumptions about security.
In 2014, Heartbleed exposed the fragility of shared infrastructure securing the internet.
In 2021, Log4Shell revealed how deeply embedded software dependencies could create widespread exposure that organizations struggled to identify.
We believe PHP2Shell could mark a similar turning point for the AI era, illustrating how AI can change the practical exploitability of longstanding vulnerabilities.
Building the exploit required chaining multiple flaws and adapting to each target’s memory layout through repeated testing and debugging.
Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours.
As the time and expertise required for this work decrease, complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier, changing how we define what is vulnerable in practice.
Wiz Research uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in core PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world.
Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them.
Sensor customers using the newest version (1.0.12768) can also enable a built-in response policy to automatically terminate processes exhibiting behaviors typical of PHP2Shell exploitation:

Wiz customers should refer to the Wiz Threat Intel Center advisory for PHP2Shell , which includes built-in coverage for agentless and runtime vulnerability detection, exploitation detection via Wiz Defend and Sensor, and automatic response policies, alongside remediation and threat hunting guidance.

These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it , putting every affected website in immediate risk.
Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4.
Below you can find a table that demonstrates what type of impact was demonstrated by each of the bugs we reported to PHP.

For over a decade, these critical vulnerabilities remained unaddressed because vulnerability discovery and exploitation were incredibly complex.

We combined these vulnerabilities into a single exploit script, php2shell, and demonstrated that it could execute code remotely without authentication on deployments of WordPress ( wordpress:latest ), Drupal ( drupal:latest ), and Joomla ( joomla:latest ), using their latest container images at the time of testing.

extraction.body: Tomorrow, First. News and intelligence for the agentic economy Two critical remote code execution flaws in the PHP language runtime, found by frontier AI models after a decade of manual audits failed to catch them, put 70% of the web on notice. Frontier AI models have identified two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities in the PHP language runtime that remained undetected through a decade of manual security audits. The vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on servers running affected versions of PHP. AI-assisted analysis identified these memory-corruption flaws, which had remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade. Wiz Research , which combined these vulnerabilities into an exploit script dubbed “php2shell,” identified the flaws as memory-safety issues stemming from how PHP handles fatal errors during request processing. CVE-2026-109618 involves out-of-memory (OOM) corruption, where PHP interrupts a request while internal data is only partially initialized. During the subsequent cleanup process, the runtime incorrectly treats this invalid data as valid. CVE-2026-109619 involves stale global state, where request-owned internal state persists after its backing memory has been freed, allowing a subsequent request handled by the same worker to utilize the stale data before it is reset. Both vulnerabilities carry a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2, marking them as critical. The flaws exploit the runtime’s trust-through-defaults pattern: the engine assumes its internal state is consistent even after an interrupted request. This pattern of implicit trust in memory management is a recurring theme in recent infrastructure vulnerabilities, similar to issues previously tracked in BeyondTrust , nine-layer , and ConnectWise . Unlike the identity-layer and supply-chain trust gaps analyzed in our prior coverage, including the synthesis in the nine-layer report, PHP2Shell represents a distinct class of failure: it sits below the application layer entirely, where the language runtime blindly trusts its own internal memory state. One brief each morning, reported by the same minds who write Forkast. Wiz Research identified these vulnerabilities using Wiz Atlas, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol. According to the firm, a single researcher completed in a week what would previously have taken a world-class team months of work. Writing in the Google Cloud post she co-authored with CISO Chris Betz, Raluca Ada Popa, Head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said Gemini 4 Argon made “an invaluable contribution to finding the vulnerability, exploit development, attack detection, and validation of the patch.” Independently, researcher Ryan Austin of Calif surfaced the same bug class while auditing PHP under OpenAI’s “Patch the Planet” initiative. Calif’s write-up of the disclosure dates the first confirmed out-of-memory fatal to August 1, days into the audit, with the first bug reported to PHP on August 11 and a working exploit confirmed by the project on August 15. Wiz Research writes that the findings “rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history,” and that demonstrating exploitability required “an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve” before frontier AI models lowered that barrier. According to Wiz Research, PHP powers 70% of all websites globally, meaning the vulnerabilities affect a significant portion of the internet. The flaws impact all currently supported PHP branches, including versions 5.4 through 8.5.11, as well as older end-of-life branches. Apache mod_php represents the highest risk surface, as the exploit can succeed before any application code executes. Other environments, including PHP-FPM, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed, are also at risk. Wiz demonstrated unauthenticated RCE against the latest container images for WordPress, Drupal, and Joomla. While Google Cloud is not itself vulnerable, the company confirmed that users running PHP on its infrastructure may be exposed. The PHP security team released patches on October 21, 2026, in versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. Because PHP 8.1 and older versions are end-of-life, the project provided only minimal source-backports for versions 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1. Administrators are advised to update immediately. For systems where immediate patching is not possible, the PHP project recommends specific mitigations: setting memory_limit to -1 to address CVE-2026-109618, and setting session.upload_progress.enabled to 0 and fatal_error_backtraces to 0 to mitigate CVE-2026-109619. While eSentire’s advisory reports unverified claims of exploit code circulating in the wild, those reports remain unconfirmed. Rapid7’s emergency threat response covers the same pair; that page returned a 403 bot wall at fetch, so it is named here rather than quoted. extraction.body: Government and company websites around the world briefly went dark and suspended some services, as operators scrambled to patch their systems after artificial intelligence helped find critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language. The US National Security Agency and Europe’s cybersecurity agency on Wednesday advised companies to take immediate action to address two critical flaws in PHP, a programming language that powers 70% of all websites in the world, including WordPress and Drupal, an open-source content management system. The PHP Foundation, the organization behind the coding language, has released a patch for the bugs, which have been hidden in their software for years, and is urging website operators to update their systems immediately. Popular Irish news website The Journal was temporarily offline Thursday morning while it bolstered its “defences,” it said in a notice. The Journal is Ireland’s second most-used online news source, behind only RTÉ, the national broadcaster, according to the Reuters Institute. The flaws in PHP – which originally stood for Personal Home Page – were uncovered by teams at OpenAI, Google-owned cybersecurity company Wiz, and another cybersecurity company, Calif. The bugs, collectively called PHP2Shell, could allow attackers to hack into websites and read memory that could contain sensitive information, like passwords. World leaders weigh in Even world leaders urged organizations to take action. Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten said that his cabinet was “closely monitoring the situation surrounding the vulnerabilities in PHP.” Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said companies should consider suspending services if necessary in order to reduce their exposure. “Please check if your publicly available websites use PHP, and prepare to apply the fix patch that will be released tonight… as soon as possible,” she posted on X Wednesday. Japanese airline ANA, railway operator JR West and the country’s largest bank, MUFG, were among companies that reported some webpages and services temporarily suspended. In Europe, government websites in France, Denmark, Finland and the Netherlands, including the Dutch cyber security agency, were temporarily taken offline while security fixes were implemented. The Wikimedia Foundation, the non-profit that operates Wikipedia, told CNN Thursday that it was “in the process of addressing security vulnerabilities in PHP,” and that a number of its systems had been taken down as a “precautionary measure.” ‘AI inflection point’ AI played a crucial role in finding and fixing vulnerabilities “that had remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade,” according to Wiz, which said the episode marks an “AI inflection point.” “What AI changed was the ability to understand the weaknesses and turn them into a working exploit,” Wiz researchers wrote in a blog post Wednesday. “With frontier AI models and the right tools, a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work,” they added. The bugs were discovered in late August but were disclosed to the public only on Wednesday, after PHP had come up with a fix. The flaws could allow attackers to remotely execute code, disrupt services and expose customer data, according to web infrastructure provider Cloudflare, which has been working with the PHP Foundation, Calif, OpenAI and Wiz to address the issue. Researchers at Wiz used Google’s Gemini 4 Argon, Wiz Atlas and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol during the research process. Heartbleed similarities Wiz researchers say the issue is on par with the Heartbleed bug from 2014, which impacted an encryption technology estimated to be used by two-thirds of the Web. Like Heartbleed, the researchers at Wiz say PHP2Shell could similarly serve as a turning point in cybersecurity. While the vulnerabilities existed for years, AI made it practical to deploy them. “The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve,” the researchers said. “Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit.” – John Liu, Anna Cooban and Amy Croffey contributed reporting.

passages: With 70% of the Internet affected, the impact of PHP2Shell cannot be overstated.
The vulnerable code had been there for more than a decade – what AI changed was the ability to understand the weaknesses and turn them into a working exploit.
With frontier AI models and the right tools, a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work.
Some vulnerabilities become turning points because they challenge fundamental assumptions about security.
In 2014, Heartbleed exposed the fragility of shared infrastructure securing the internet.
In 2021, Log4Shell revealed how deeply embedded software dependencies could create widespread exposure that organizations struggled to identify.
We believe PHP2Shell could mark a similar turning point for the AI era, illustrating how AI can change the practical exploitability of longstanding vulnerabilities.
Building the exploit required chaining multiple flaws and adapting to each target’s memory layout through repeated testing and debugging.
Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours.
As the time and expertise required for this work decrease, complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier, changing how we define what is vulnerable in practice.
Wiz Research uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in core PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world.
Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them.
Sensor customers using the newest version (1.0.12768) can also enable a built-in response policy to automatically terminate processes exhibiting behaviors typical of PHP2Shell exploitation:

Wiz customers should refer to the Wiz Threat Intel Center advisory for PHP2Shell , which includes built-in coverage for agentless and runtime vulnerability detection, exploitation detection via Wiz Defend and Sensor, and automatic response policies, alongside remediation and threat hunting guidance.

These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it , putting every affected website in immediate risk.
Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4.

extraction.body: Core PHP engine flaws enable remote code execution and Heartbleed-style memory disclosure across the web. Wiz Research uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in core PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world. Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them. PHP is a backbone of the web: it’s the programming language powering WordPress, Joomla, Drupal, Wikipedia’s MediaWiki, and many others. These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it , putting every affected website in immediate risk. Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4. Attackers can exploit them remotely, in some cases fairly easily. Immediate patching is strongly advised. On October 21, 2026, PHP released the patch fixing multiple memory-safety vulnerabilities in the core engine. These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history. The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit. In this post, we explain how frontier AI helped us find and fix vulnerabilities that had remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade. The issues described below all stem from key architecture decisions, some made over a decade ago, and were grouped under two CVEs, with severity reaching CVSS 9.2. The work grew into a cross-industry effort to protect customers, find variants, deploy detections and mitigations, and verify a patch in time for coordinated disclosure. Nearly every PHP version is affected by at least one of these issues, including releases dating back to PHP 5.4. The vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on affected servers or read sensitive process memory. That memory may contain passwords, authentication tokens, API keys and certificates belonging to other requests or the server itself. PHP is the programming language behind much of the web, powering WordPress, Drupal and MediaWiki, the software that runs Wikipedia. A flaw in its core engine can affect websites across this ecosystem, even when their own application code is secure. Some vulnerabilities become turning points because they challenge fundamental assumptions about security. In 2014, Heartbleed exposed the fragility of shared infrastructure securing the internet. In 2021, Log4Shell revealed how deeply embedded software dependencies could create widespread exposure that organizations struggled to identify. We believe PHP2Shell could mark a similar turning point for the AI era, illustrating how AI can change the practical exploitability of longstanding vulnerabilities. Building the exploit required chaining multiple flaws and adapting to each target’s memory layout through repeated testing and debugging. Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours. As the time and expertise required for this work decrease, complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier, changing how we define what is vulnerable in practice. Wiz Research would like to thank the PHP team, Calif and OpenAI for their work on discovery, coordination and patch verification. OpenAI and Calif also published blogs containing details on the vulnerability – its history, technical details, and insight into the disclosure process. PHP posted as well. We’d also like to express our sincere gratitude towards Automattic, Akamai, AWS, Cloudflare , Fastly , Google , Imperva, Microsoft, Vercel , and many others, for helping prepare guidance and out-of-the-box mitigations for customers who cannot apply the patch immediately. All of the disclosed vulnerabilities are memory-safety issues that stem from bugs in how PHP handles fatal errors while processing requests, particularly out-of-memory errors. These bugs can leave a corrupted internal PHP state behind after a request ends unexpectedly. A later request or worker can reuse that stale state, leading to memory disclosure or corruption. Below you can find a table that demonstrates what type of impact was demonstrated by each of the bugs we reported to PHP. The applications listed below are targets we chose for the RCE demonstrations. They are representative targets - exploitation does not require one of these CMSs, as the vulnerable code is in PHP itself. While this blog covers only four instances of exploitable bugs (grouped under two CVEs) that follow this problematic pattern, there are other tracked, and likely untracked, variants of this issue in the PHP codebase. These variants have different requirements for exploitation and can lead to different types of impact. In any case, the patch provided by the PHP team fixes the issue at its core and eliminates all variants in the patched release. We combined these vulnerabilities into a single exploit script, php2shell, and demonstrated that it could execute code remotely without authentication on deployments of WordPress ( wordpress:latest ), Drupal ( drupal:latest ), and Joomla ( joomla:latest ), using their latest container images at the time of testing. These platforms illustrate the impact, but the vulnerabilities are in PHP itself. Exploitation does not depend on a flaw in the application’s code: even a simple “Hello World” application running on an affected PHP version can be vulnerable. Separately, we demonstrated that attackers could read sensitive data from the PHP process’s memory, including passwords, tokens, and API keys, without needing to achieve remote code execution. Demonstrations of PHP2Shell with Wordpress, Joomla, and Drupal: With AI this is no longer a barrier. LLMs can help adapt an exploit to different PHP versions, configurations and memory layouts. With testing and debugging tools, models can analyze failures and iterate on adjustments, reducing the specialist effort required for each target. This significantly lowers the barrier to scaling attacks across different deployments. This changes the economics of both discovery and exploitation. As AI reduces the effort needed to develop and adapt complex exploits, vulnerabilities that once seemed impractical to exploit become viable targets. We used Wiz Atlas , Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol throughout this research. Notably, Gemini 4 Argon made an invaluable contribution to finding the vulnerability, exploit development, attack detection, and validation of the patch. Using Gemini 4 Argon, the team at Wiz has shown why frontier AI is a game-changer for cyber defense. For over a decade, these critical vulnerabilities remained unaddressed because vulnerability discovery and exploitation were incredibly complex. We're pleased to see Gemini 4 Argon help defenders bridge that gap, finding vulnerabilities and helping patch them. Prior to public disclosure, Wiz Research worked with the PHP team, Calif and OpenAI on discovery, coordination and patch verification. We also partnered with Google Cloud, Cloudflare, AWS, Microsoft, Automattic, Fastly, Akamai, Imperva, Vercel and many others to prepare customer guidance, detections and out-of-the-box mitigations for organizations that cannot update immediately. There are other variants outside of these four bugs. While we initially reported these four to PHP, through this research we realized the vulnerability is deeply rooted in the PHP codebase and will require a comprehensive fix. Other variants should also fold under the same two CVEs. Wiz customers should refer to the Wiz Threat Intel Center advisory for PHP2Shell , which includes built-in coverage for agentless and runtime vulnerability detection, exploitation detection via Wiz Defend and Sensor, and automatic response policies, alongside remediation and threat hunting guidance. Sensor customers using the newest version (1.0.12768) can also enable a built-in response policy to automatically terminate processes exhibiting behaviors typical of PHP2Shell exploitation: With 70% of the Internet affected, the impact of PHP2Shell cannot be overstated. It marks an AI inflection point. The vulnerable code had been there for more than a decade – what AI changed was the ability to understand the weaknesses and turn them into a working exploit. With frontier AI models and the right tools, a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work. This changes the economics of both discovery and exploitation. Vulnerabilities that once seemed impractical to exploit become viable targets. These same capabilities also give defenders a chance to uncover and fix flaws that have survived years of scrutiny. Wiz used Wiz Atlas, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol throughout this research, with Argon making a particularly significant contribution to finding and helping to remediate the vulnerability. August 21, 2026: Unauthenticated RCE is confirmed against WordPress. August 24, 2026: Wiz Research reports the vulnerabilities to the PHP security team. September 21, 2026: PHP acknowledges the reports and begins developing a coordinated fix. Wiz researchers will walk through what we've discovered, how we found these vulnerabilities, and what security teams need to know to assess their exposure and respond. In a new incident, a malicious version (1.107.0) of the LiteLLM package was uploaded to PyPI and Docker on October 21. The malicious version includes a credential stealer targeting browser, cloud and AI secrets as well as a dormant C2 capability.

Separately, we demonstrated that attackers could read sensitive data from the PHP process’s memory, including passwords, tokens, and API keys, without needing to achieve remote code execution.

With testing and debugging tools, models can analyze failures and iterate on adjustments, reducing the specialist effort required for each target. This significantly lowers the barrier to scaling attacks across different deployments.

This changes the economics of both discovery and exploitation. As AI reduces the effort needed to develop and adapt complex exploits, vulnerabilities that once seemed impractical to exploit become viable targets.

We used Wiz Atlas , Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol throughout this research. Notably, Gemini 4 Argon made an invaluable contribution to finding the vulnerability, exploit development, attack detection, and validation of the patch.

Using Gemini 4 Argon, the team at Wiz has shown why frontier AI is a game-changer for cyber defense. For over a decade, these critical vulnerabilities remained unaddressed because vulnerability discovery and exploitation were incredibly complex. We're pleased to see Gemini 4 Argon help defenders bridge that gap, finding vulnerabilities and helping patch them.

Prior to public disclosure, Wiz Research worked with the PHP team, Calif and OpenAI on discovery, coordination and patch verification. We also partnered with Google Cloud, Cloudflare, AWS, Microsoft, Automattic, Fastly, Akamai, Imperva, Vercel and many others to prepare customer guidance, detections and out-of-the-box mitigations for organizations that cannot update immediately.

This changes the economics of both discovery and exploitation. Vulnerabilities that once seemed impractical to exploit become viable targets. These same capabilities also give defenders a chance to uncover and fix flaws that have survived years of scrutiny.
Wiz used Wiz Atlas, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol throughout this research, with Argon making a particularly significant contribution to finding and helping to remediate the vulnerability.

passages: Meta is making a big push into AI, and it’s creating a new kind of stock that could help pay for it.

On Wednesday, as the company reported its third-quarter earnings, Semafor reported the company might issue non-voting stock, meaning shares that don’t give their owners a vote on company decisions, to help fund its push into artificial intelligence.

During Meta’s earnings call, the company confirmed that reporting. Meta’s chief financial officer, Susan Li, said the company plans to “create a new class of non-voting capital stock, which will be distributed to all existing shareholders through a stock dividend.”

Li later added that the company “created this new class of shares with the purpose of creating a publicly traded non-voting stock usable for capital raising, employee compensation, acquisitions, and other general corporate purposes while preserving the voting power of existing Class A and B shareholders.”

The shares will allow the company to maintain its current “founder-led structure,” she added. They will also expand its “funding tools and give us flexibility to invest behind the unprecedented momentum we’re seeing across every part of our business, driven by AI.”

Meta’s earnings were strong this past quarter, beating Wall Street expectations. The company made $64 billion in revenue, a jump of 26% from a year earlier. Its costs and expenses also rose too, however, by 68% year over year.

Reality Labs, the division responsible for Meta’s AR glasses, VR headsets, and VR software, continues to lose money, though less than it used to. The company said in its earnings report that it expects the division’s losses to shrink from its 2025 levels to between $18 billion and $19 billion.

Meta has made a big push into AI over the past year. The company has released several AI models, including Muse Spark and Muse Glimmer earlier this year. In recent weeks, it added Muse Wonder and Muse Spark Open, an open-weight model whose underlying parameters are publicly available for outsiders to use and build on. Meta also launched a coding agent for software developers called Muse Code. At its Meta Connect event this year, the company announced a new line of cute and cuddly avatars for AI assistant, Meta Muse, in a push to make its AI services more relatable (and also meme-able ).

As far as can be discerned, those AI products are doing well. “In just a month and a half, more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada have set up Muse personal agents,” CEO Mark Zuckerberg said during Wednesday’s earnings call. “Growth continues to be strong, and we have been number one in the App Store almost every day.”

“Now that Muse has clear product-market fit, we are entering a new phase and a more operational phase that is focused on scaling it,” Zuckerberg added, claiming later that the company expects to grow the product’s appeal to eventually “serve billions of people.”

The company also noted that certain storm clouds linger on the horizon in the form of ongoing regulatory and legal issues. “We continue to monitor active legal and regulatory matters that could significantly impact our business and financial results,” said Li. “For example, we continue to see scrutiny on youth-related issues in several markets, and have a number of youth-related trials scheduled in the coming months in the United States.”

Meta said the shares let it raise capital, pay employees and fund acquisitions without diluting voting power, and Meta said it expects to sell Class C stock from time to time.

Meta also said it expects to sell Class C stock from time to time, while Benzinga reported that Meta’s third-quarter revenue was $64.6 billion, beating analyst estimates of $63.37 billion, and that adjusted earnings were $7.40 per share.

Meta’s plan arrived alongside a capital-spend outlook that Nicholas Mugalli, CEO and principal of World Trade Securities, described as a sign of “more capex coming,” with 2026 capex already guided at $135 billion to $145 billion.
Meta reported net income of $9.860 billion, or $3.83 a diluted share, for the quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with $2.709 billion, or $1.05 a share, a year earlier.

Meta said the agreement provided for payments of up to about $18.59 billion, while the charge recognized in the third quarter was the lower $9.89 billion amount.

coreStoryFacts.text: Meta is making a big push into AI, and it’s creating a new kind of stock that could help pay for it.
During Meta’s earnings call, the company confirmed that reporting.

Li later added that the company “created this new class of shares with the purpose of creating a publicly traded non-voting stock usable for capital raising, employee compensation, acquisitions, and other general corporate purposes while preserving the voting power of existing Class A and B shareholders.”
The company made $64 billion in revenue, a jump of 26% from a year earlier.
Its costs and expenses also rose too, however, by 68% year over year.
The company has released several AI models, including Muse Spark and Muse Glimmer earlier this year.
Meta also launched a coding agent for software developers called Muse Code.

Meta’s spending plans also reached beyond its own balance sheet, and Startup Fortune said Meta tried this exact move once before in 2016, proposing a Class C stock so Zuckerberg could keep control while giving away shares through the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative.

Meta said it expects its Class A share price to reflect the effect of a two-for-one stock split after the payment, while BigGo Finance said free cash flow turned negative at $2.12 billion, compared with positive $10.63 billion a year earlier.

Meta said the Class C shares carry no voting rights, and the company said shareholders won’t vote on the change because entities tied to Mark Zuckerberg and his wife, Priscilla Chan, that hold 56.1% of Meta’s voting power approved it on Tuesday.

Meta’s plan arrived alongside a capital-spend outlook that Nicholas Mugalli, CEO and principal of World Trade Securities, described as a sign of “more capex coming,” with 2026 capex already guided at $135 billion to $145 billion.

During Meta’s earnings call, the company confirmed that reporting. Meta’s chief financial officer, Susan Li, said the company plans to “create a new class of non-voting capital stock, which will be distributed to all existing shareholders through a stock dividend.” Li later added that the company “created this new class of shares with the purpose of creating a publicly traded non-voting stock usable for capital raising, employee compensation, acquisitions, and other general corporate purposes while preserving the voting power of existing Class A and B shareholders.” The shares will allow the company to maintain its current “founder-led structure,” she added. passages: Meta is making a big push into AI, and it’s creating a new kind of stock that could help pay for it.

On Wednesday, as the company reported its third-quarter earnings, Semafor reported the company might issue non-voting stock, meaning shares that don’t give their owners a vote on company decisions, to help fund its push into artificial intelligence.

During Meta’s earnings call, the company confirmed that reporting. Meta’s chief financial officer, Susan Li, said the company plans to “create a new class of non-voting capital stock, which will be distributed to all existing shareholders through a stock dividend.”

Li later added that the company “created this new class of shares with the purpose of creating a publicly traded non-voting stock usable for capital raising, employee compensation, acquisitions, and other general corporate purposes while preserving the voting power of existing Class A and B shareholders.”

The shares will allow the company to maintain its current “founder-led structure,” she added. They will also expand its “funding tools and give us flexibility to invest behind the unprecedented momentum we’re seeing across every part of our business, driven by AI.”

Meta’s earnings were strong this past quarter, beating Wall Street expectations. The company made $64 billion in revenue, a jump of 26% from a year earlier. Its costs and expenses also rose too, however, by 68% year over year.

Reality Labs, the division responsible for Meta’s AR glasses, VR headsets, and VR software, continues to lose money, though less than it used to. The company said in its earnings report that it expects the division’s losses to shrink from its 2025 levels to between $18 billion and $19 billion.

Meta has made a big push into AI over the past year. The company has released several AI models, including Muse Spark and Muse Glimmer earlier this year. In recent weeks, it added Muse Wonder and Muse Spark Open, an open-weight model whose underlying parameters are publicly available for outsiders to use and build on. Meta also launched a coding agent for software developers called Muse Code. At its Meta Connect event this year, the company announced a new line of cute and cuddly avatars for AI assistant, Meta Muse, in a push to make its AI services more relatable (and also meme-able ).

As far as can be discerned, those AI products are doing well. “In just a month and a half, more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada have set up Muse personal agents,” CEO Mark Zuckerberg said during Wednesday’s earnings call. “Growth continues to be strong, and we have been number one in the App Store almost every day.”

“Now that Muse has clear product-market fit, we are entering a new phase and a more operational phase that is focused on scaling it,” Zuckerberg added, claiming later that the company expects to grow the product’s appeal to eventually “serve billions of people.”

The company also noted that certain storm clouds linger on the horizon in the form of ongoing regulatory and legal issues. “We continue to monitor active legal and regulatory matters that could significantly impact our business and financial results,” said Li. “For example, we continue to see scrutiny on youth-related issues in several markets, and have a number of youth-related trials scheduled in the coming months in the United States.”

Meta said the Class C shares carry no voting rights, and the company said shareholders won’t vote on the change because entities tied to Mark Zuckerberg and his wife, Priscilla Chan, that hold 56.1% of Meta’s voting power approved it on Tuesday. Meta’s plan arrived alongside a capital-spend outlook that Nicholas Mugalli, CEO and principal of World Trade Securities, described as a sign of “more capex coming,” with 2026 capex already guided at $135 billion to $145 billion. Meta reported net income of $9.860 billion, or $3.83 a diluted share, for the quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with $2.709 billion, or $1.05 a share, a year earlier. Meta said its reported profit was heavily affected by a $9.89 billion legal-proceedings charge tied to its August agreement with 52 U.S. attorneys general over litigation concerning teen mental health and social media. Meta said the agreement provided for payments of up to about $18.59 billion, while the charge recognized in the third quarter was the lower $9.89 billion amount. Meta Platforms said its board declared a dividend of one share of Class C common stock for each outstanding share of Class A and Class B common stock as part of a recapitalization that takes effect Jan. 19, 2027.

Meta said the Class C shares carry no voting rights, and the company said shareholders won’t vote on the change because entities tied to Mark Zuckerberg and his wife, Priscilla Chan, that hold 56.1% of Meta’s voting power approved it on Tuesday.
Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan-linked holders approved the change
Meta said the shares let it raise capital, pay employees and fund acquisitions without diluting voting power, and Meta said it expects to sell Class C stock from time to time.

Meta also said it expects to sell Class C stock from time to time, while Benzinga reported that Meta’s third-quarter revenue was $64.6 billion, beating analyst estimates of $63.37 billion, and that adjusted earnings were $7.40 per share.

Meta’s plan arrived alongside a capital-spend outlook that Nicholas Mugalli, CEO and principal of World Trade Securities, described as a sign of “more capex coming,” with 2026 capex already guided at $135 billion to $145 billion.
Meta reported net income of $9.860 billion, or $3.83 a diluted share, for the quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with $2.709 billion, or $1.05 a share, a year earlier.

Meta said its reported profit was heavily affected by a $9.89 billion legal-proceedings charge tied to its August agreement with 52 U.S. attorneys general over litigation concerning teen mental health and social media.
Meta said the agreement provided for payments of up to about $18.59 billion, while the charge recognized in the third quarter was the lower $9.89 billion amount.

Meta said operating income was $12.988 billion, down 37% from the prior-year quarter, as costs and expenses rose 68% to $51.613 billion, and it said excluding the charge operating income would have been $22.88 billion and diluted earnings per share would have been $7.40.

Meta also said it expects fourth-quarter revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion versus estimates of $73.74 billion, and it said it narrowed its 2026 capital-expenditure outlook to $135 billion to $145 billion.

Meta said capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, totaled $34.91 billion in the third quarter, and FindArticles said the company’s midpoint of its new full-year capital-expenditure range is $140 billion. Meta’s spending plans also reached beyond its own balance sheet, and Startup Fortune said Meta tried this exact move once before in 2016, proposing a Class C stock so Zuckerberg could keep control while giving away shares through the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. Startup Fortune said shareholders sued, and Meta abandoned that plan in 2017, while it said a decade later Meta paired the new structure with a Founder Alignment Agreement signed October 20 that restricts Zuckerberg from selling Class C shares without a matching cut to his own voting power.

Meta said it expects its Class A share price to reflect the effect of a two-for-one stock split after the payment, while BigGo Finance said free cash flow turned negative at $2.12 billion, compared with positive $10.63 billion a year earlier. Meta’s board said the Class C shares would be usable for capital raising, employee compensation, acquisitions and other general corporate purposes, and TechCrunch said Meta’s chief financial officer, Susan Li, said the company plans to “create a new class of non-voting capital stock, which will be distributed to all existing shareholders through a stock dividend.”

Meta reportedly plans to create a new class of non-voting stock. The goal is to sell shares to fund AI development without touching Mark Zuckerberg’s grip on the company. 
 Meta has not officially confirmed any plans for an equity issuance. The plan, if it happens, would mark a notable shift in how the company pays for one of the most expensive bets in corporate history. 
 

 Why Meta needs the money 
 Meta anticipates capital expenditures of between $130 billion and $145 billion for AI-related projects by 2026. 
 Most of that money is aimed at data centers and other technological infrastructure. These are the server farms and computing clusters that train and run large AI models. 
 Until now, Meta has paid for this buildout mostly through debt and operating cash flow. It has avoided large equity sales. 
 That possibility has fueled market chatter about a potential “monster secondary” offering. A secondary offering is when a company sells additional shares to the public after its initial listing, which raises cash but spreads ownership across more shares.

A non-voting class sidesteps the problem entirely. New investors would add capital, and the voting math would stay where it is. The most direct impact would land on existing investors. A large equity sale would spread Meta’s earnings across a bigger share count, and the non-voting format means new buyers would carry economic risk without any governance power. When a company commits to spending of between $130 billion and $145 billion, shareholders typically want a mechanism to push back if returns disappoint. A non-voting class removes that lever for the newest money coming in. There is also a funding-mix question worth watching.  Meta has not officially confirmed any plans for an equity issuance. The plan, if it happens, would mark a notable shift in how the company pays for one of the most expensive bets in corporate history. 
 

 Why Meta needs the money 
 Meta anticipates capital expenditures of between $130 billion and $145 billion for AI-related projects by 2026. 
 Most of that money is aimed at data centers and other technological infrastructure. These are the server farms and computing clusters that train and run large AI models. 
 Until now, Meta has paid for this buildout mostly through debt and operating cash flow. It has avoided large equity sales. 
 That possibility has fueled market chatter about a potential “monster secondary” offering. A secondary offering is when a company sells additional shares to the public after its initial listing, which raises cash but spreads ownership across more shares.

Meta reportedly plans to create a new class of non-voting stock. The goal is to sell shares to fund AI development without touching Mark Zuckerberg’s grip on the company.

Meta has not officially confirmed any plans for an equity issuance. The plan, if it happens, would mark a notable shift in how the company pays for one of the most expensive bets in corporate history.
Meta anticipates capital expenditures of between $130 billion and $145 billion for AI-related projects by 2026.
Most of that money is aimed at data centers and other technological infrastructure. These are the server farms and computing clusters that train and run large AI models.
Until now, Meta has paid for this buildout mostly through debt and operating cash flow. It has avoided large equity sales.

That possibility has fueled market chatter about a potential “monster secondary” offering. A secondary offering is when a company sells additional shares to the public after its initial listing, which raises cash but spreads ownership across more shares.
The non-voting structure exists for a specific reason. It lets Meta issue stock without diluting Zuckerberg’s voting power.
As of mid-2026, Zuckerberg holds approximately 61% of voting power . He owns only around 13.5% of the company’s economic shares .

That gap is the product of Meta’s existing dual-class structure. Some shares carry more votes than others, which allows a founder to steer the company while owning a minority of its value.
A non-voting class sidesteps the problem entirely. New investors would add capital, and the voting math would stay where it is.

The most direct impact would land on existing investors. A large equity sale would spread Meta’s earnings across a bigger share count, and the non-voting format means new buyers would carry economic risk without any governance power.

When a company commits to spending of between $130 billion and $145 billion, shareholders typically want a mechanism to push back if returns disappoint. A non-voting class removes that lever for the newest money coming in.

There is also a funding-mix question worth watching. Meta has leaned on debt and cash flow so far, and a pivot toward equity could signal that management expects the buildout to outrun what those sources can comfortably cover.
The key things to track now are whether Meta formally confirms the share class, how large any eventual offering turns out to be, and whether short interest keeps climbing.

passages: J.P. Morgan just named Bitcoin the highest-returning asset in its long-term outlook, and that changes the math on even a small stake in ways most investors have not considered.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
A stake of 0.1 Bitcoin ( CRYPTO: BTC ) is valued at approximately $8,332. At J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s expected 10% annual return, this amount could rise to roughly $12,426 by the end of 2030.

Buying 0.1 Bitcoin is a practical choice for average investors, whether they purchase it outright or accumulate it gradually through dollar-cost averaging, which involves investing a set amount regularly, irrespective of the coin’s price fluctuations.

Bitcoin is currently trading around $83,316, up 2.1% over the past 24 hours. It has risen 27.7% over the last three months, though it remains down 23.4% compared to a year ago. Since late September, Bitcoin’s price has fluctuated, reaching around $87,283 on September 23 and dropping to about $79,676 by October 15.

J.P. Morgan’s latest insights come from its 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions, which predict Bitcoin will deliver a 10% compound annual return over the next 10 to 15 years—the highest among all assets in the report. So, what could 0.1 Bitcoin be worth in 2030, and what scenarios should you consider?

If Bitcoin grows at an average of 10% annually for the roughly 4.2 years remaining until 2030, it could reach about $124,265. This is just shy of its previous peak of $126,080 recorded on October 6, 2025. J.P. Morgan’s growth projection suggests Bitcoin could return to those highs within the next four years.

However, it’s essential to understand that J.P. Morgan’s projection is an average, so it can include significant downturns. For example, Bitcoin hit a monthly low of $58,000 in June 2026, and Michael Saylor, Strategy Executive Chairman, noted on October 13 that he thinks the bottom was slightly below $60,000.

At $200,000, Bitcoin’s market capitalization—calculated by multiplying its price by the total number of coins mined—could soar to about $4.02 trillion. Because miners continuously produce new coins, reaching any target price in 2030 will require more total investment than we see today.

Spot Bitcoin ETFs , exchange-traded funds that hold Bitcoin directly and trade like stocks, have grown notably. As of October 20, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs reported $106.28 billion in total net assets, with cumulative net inflows of $57.43 billion.

However, ETF flows have been inconsistent. On September 21, funds saw an influx of $999 million—the largest one-day gain in the previous month—only to lose $487.1 million a few weeks later. On October 20, funds added a modest $23.2 million.
The launch of spot Bitcoin ETFs in January 2024 hints at what demand could look like if all goes well; Bitcoin’s price surged from around $42,611 at the end of January 2024 to $73,628 by March .

Moreover, the Department of Labor proposed a rule on March 30, 2026, that could allow 401(k) plans to include alternative assets, including cryptocurrencies. While still under consideration, this proposal could unlock new avenues for investment. Employers will ultimately decide what their plans offer, so some may hesitate because of potential litigation risks.

Institutional interest is also growing. Investor Moez Kassam mentioned on The Pomp Podcast on October 20 that large investors are increasingly accepting Bitcoin as a viable asset, further solidifying its place in the financial landscape.

We believe 0.1 Bitcoin has a reasonable chance of reaching around $12,426 by the end of 2030, while $20,000 seems unlikely. J.P. Morgan’s projected pace only requires Bitcoin to return to its previous record high, while the bullish scenario suggests a significant increase in the entire network’s value, reaching $4.02 trillion.

Reaching these levels will depend on Bitcoin first recovering its September high of $87,397 and ETF assets surpassing their September 22 peak of $110.84 billion . If a final rule for the 401(k) and a breakout above the record high occur, the $200,000 mark could become a possibility. Conversely, if ETF demand declines and proposals stall, Bitcoin could retest the $60,000 level, leaving 0.1 Bitcoin worth $6,000. A drop below the June low of $58,000 would invalidate Saylor’s bottom call and could lead to a more pessimistic outlook for Bitcoin as we approach 2030.

But these bull and bear cycles are common with the crypto market. If you take a long-term view, Bitcoin's performance looks much better. It's up 421% over the last three years, well ahead of the S&P 500 's 80% return. While cryptocurrencies are volatile, this also means they have the potential to explode in value , turning even small investments into much larger amounts. With that in mind, let's consider what a $1 Bitcoin investment today could be worth in 2030. There have been a range of predictions for what Bitcoin will be worth at the end of the decade. British bank Standard Chartered projects that Bitcoin's price will reach $500,000 in 2030. Multiple prominent figures, including Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong and Block CEO Jack Dorsey, have expressed their belief that it could reach $1 million or more. Ark Invest founder, CEO, and chief investment officer Cathie Wood has a price target of $1.2 million for the leading cryptocurrency. These are all bullish predictions, and they aren't exactly set in stone. Standard Chartered and Cathie Wood have both adjusted their price targets downwards recently due to the decline in Bitcoin's price. Another option is to examine Bitcoin's past performance. It had a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 93% from August 2011 to November 2025. If it averages that annual return over the next four years, it will be worth $1.2 million, exactly what Wood is now predicting. Bitcoin currently has a price of about $87,000. If it grows to between $500,000 and $1 million in 2030, then a $1 investment in Bitcoin today would be worth anywhere from about $5.75 to $11.50. It's also possible that Bitcoin will achieve only modest growth or even decline over the next few years. Despite its success, Bitcoin remains a risky and volatile asset. While I think it's likely Bitcoin continues to increase in value, I wouldn't bet the farm on it. That's why Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies generally shouldn't make up more than 5% of your portfolio. Bitcoin is past the stage where a $1 investment will become a large amount of money. The only cryptocurrencies that could do that are much smaller coins, and it takes quite a bit of luck to pick out which of these will succeed, as most don't. However, you can build a crypto portfolio on a reasonable budget. One approach to consider is dollar-cost averaging , where you invest a consistent amount into cryptocurrencies you like at regular intervals. For example, you could invest $100 per week or month. This is a good way to establish a solid position in Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies over time. There have been a range of predictions for what Bitcoin will be worth at the end of the decade.
British bank Standard Chartered projects that Bitcoin's price will reach $500,000 in 2030.
Multiple prominent figures, including Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong and Block CEO Jack Dorsey, have expressed their belief that it could reach $1 million or more.
The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Bitcoin and Block.
Analysts have set ambitious price targets for Bitcoin in 2030.
Let's see what that could mean for a small investment in the leading cryptocurrency.
Bitcoin is past the stage where a $1 investment will become a large amount of money.
The only cryptocurrencies that could do that are much smaller coins, and it takes quite a bit of luck to pick out which of these will succeed, as most don't.
